The subsequent global stage, based on this threshold, refines the solution. To achieve scalability and robustness, we draw on principles from control theory and embed QuantGraph's global stage within a receding-horizon model-predictive-control scheme. This classical layer stabilizes and guides the quantum search, improving precision and reducing computational burden. In practice, the resulting closed-loop system exhibits robust behavior and lower query complexity. Notably, for a fixed control horizon and query budget, QuantGraph supports approximately twice as many control discretization bits while still benefiting from Grover-search's inherent quadratic speedup compared to classical methods.
Quantum Physics.comment: P. Vaidhyanathan and A. Papatheodorou contributed equally to this work. Published in Physical Review Applied. 17 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables, 2 algorithms

Quantum Physics.title: Bottom-Up Design of Quantum Optical Experiments Using Discrete Generative Models
Quantum Physics.summary: Designing quantum optical experiments requires searching over discrete circuit topologies and continuous parameters, often leading to multiple possible realizations of the same target state. Graph-based methods commonly address this problem by optimizing a dense graph and pruning it toward a single circuit. We introduce \texttt{Grinch}, a bottom-up reward-driven generative framework that learns to sample optical graphs directly from fidelity-based rewards without relying on a pre-existing training dataset. We demonstrate the framework on multipartite entangled states, graph and cluster states, and nonlocal photonic-gate targets, obtaining multiple high-fidelity optical graphs. For nonlocal photonic gates, we obtain Toffoli constructions requiring two ancillas and alternative CNOT and Toffoli designs when connections between ancilla nodes are restricted. For state preparation, we identify asymptotic solutions for targets that cannot be generated exactly by graphs. Using the discovered topologies, we derive analytic families of optical experiments with explicit interference mechanisms and fidelity--rate relations, showing how generative design can support interpretable scientific discovery. These findings illustrate a reward-driven approach to quantum optical inverse design, exploring alternative circuit topologies while directly incorporating connectivity constraints into the search process.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Material Generation via Coherent Hamiltonian Search
Quantum Physics.summary: Discovering new materials with targeted properties is a central goal of materials science, yet the space of candidates is vast. Data-driven generative models learn the distribution of known materials, but they extrapolate poorly, and a generated structure is not known to be stable. A material's properties follow from its Hamiltonian, and a quantum computer can calculate them from it. We introduce the quantum material generative algorithm (QMage), a coherent search, guided by the Hamiltonian, over crystalline configurations of atomic composition, unit cell structure, and atomic positions, for one whose calculated properties meet the targets to within a given error tolerance. The computation is a single coherent quantum circuit in which each configuration's Hamiltonian is block-encoded, its target eigenstate isolated and properties evaluated, and the satisfying configurations amplified by fixed-point search and measured. One framework covers many targets, from formation energy and band gaps to elasticity and conductivity. We design the algorithm for the mature fault-tolerant era and estimate its cost in logical qubits and Toffoli depth from a classically routine benchmark to targets where established methods are unreliable. The approach generates candidate materials from first principles, rather than generalizing from those known, and could enable materials discovery when the target properties are difficult to predict classically.

Quantum Physics.title: The importance of shear strain in narrow Si/SiGe quantum wells
Quantum Physics.summary: Several heterostructure profiles have been proposed for Si/SiGe quantum wells, to improve the operation of quantum-dot spin qubits. These structures share a common goal of generating either of the two wave vectors that govern the conduction-band valley coupling, dubbed $k_0$ and $k_1$. Here, we focus on the long-wavelength $k_1$ term that couples valleys when paired with shear strain, and which governs the Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling. We show that shear strain induced by metal top gates may be enough to activate the $k_1$ valley-coupling mechanism, mitigating the need for "ultrasharp" interfaces, as commonly assumed for large valley energy splittings. We propose a scheme featuring narrow quantum wells that does not require ultrasharp interfaces, but should still provide large deterministic valley splittings (when paired with shear strain), and large spin-orbit couplings and $g$-factor corrections, which are of great interest for experimental implementations.

Quantum Physics.title: Communication inequalities: robust quantum advantage, measurement testing and dimension witnessing with minimal setups
Quantum Physics.summary: Communication scenarios (CS) are arguably the simplest setting in which quantum behaviors can be observed. Yet, in contrast to Bell scenarios or prepare-measure scenarios with shared randomness, no general method is known to separate classical and quantum statistics. Here we close this gap by deriving dimensional inequalities to separate classical and quantum statistics in CS. These depend only on four parameters of the input-output statistics, corresponding to correlated and anticorrelated events. Under dimensional assumptions, saturating one of the inequalities certifies SIC-POVMs with analytical noise robustness. The inequalities also yield a dimension witness for both correlated and anti-correlated statistics, without the need of measurement incompatibility.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum geometric bounds and uncertainty relations for velocity variance and spread of Wannier function
Quantum Physics.summary: By utilizing the derivation of quantum Cramér-Rao bound and an argument put forward by Efimov and Dodonov, we derive several uncertainty relations for mixed states that constrain the diagonal product, trace, and each diagonal element of the covariance matrix of multiple observables. By choosing the observables to be the symmetric logarithmic derivative, the uncertainty relations imply various geometric bounds on quantum Fisher information matrix caused by mean Uhlmann curvature, which in pure states become geometric bounds on quantum metric caused by Berry curvature. Our formalism reveals optical sum rules for velocity variance and spread of valence band Wannier functions, and how they are bounded by the Berry curvature and commutator of velocity operators. Canonical ensembles of spins, topological materials, common semiconductors, and transition metal dichalcogenides are used to verify these geometric bounds and uncertainty relations.

Quantum Physics.title: Comprehensive quantum electrodynamics of fast electrons interacting with dissipative nanostructures and quantum light
Quantum Physics.summary: Theoretical descriptions of the quantum electrodynamical interaction between fast electrons and nanostructures conventionally rely on standard macroscopic quantum electrodynamics (MQED), which, when applied to bounded objects in vacuum, formally requires an asymptotic limiting procedure to account for free-space radiation modes. To explicitly incorporate these modes from the outset, we employ the modified Langevin noise formalism (MLNF), which independently quantizes both the asymptotic scattering modes and the electromagnetic field generated by dissipative material sources. Utilizing an exact second-order Magnus expansion, we derive a closed-form, nonperturbative master formula for the transverse-momentum-resolved energy exchange probability. In the unilluminated regime, we demonstrate that at finite nanostructure temperatures, the vacuum scattering and thermal material fluctuations do not mathematically recombine into the total imaginary part of the dyadic Green's function. This breakdown does not violate the Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem, because the explicit zero-temperature scattering field acts as an independent dynamical system that maintains the configuration out of global thermodynamic equilibrium. This fundamental separation reveals an intrinsic Stokes--Anti-Stokes asymmetry, yielding distinct transverse diffraction patterns for energy loss and thermal energy gain, and establishing a generalized detailed-balance relation that governs the radiative reduction of the apparent temperature in nanoscale electron thermometry. In the illuminated regime, our framework rigorously incorporates quantum-optical states into macroscopic dissipative electrodynamics, demonstrating that...

Quantum Physics.title: Enhancing valley splitting in Si/SiGe Wiggle Well quantum dots through integrated stressor-gate architectures
Quantum Physics.summary: Engineering large and reproducible valley splittings is essential for the scalable operation of silicon spin qubits. In Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, valley splitting arises predominantly from atomic-scale disorder and is therefore inherently random, motivating approaches that introduce a large deterministic contribution. Strain-assisted Wiggle Wells provide a route to deterministic valley splitting by combining an oscillatory Ge concentration in the Si well with shear strain; however, generating the required strain in a manner compatible with large-scale architectures remains a challenge. Here, we propose patterned stressed thin films as a scalable approach for generating shear strain in the quantum well of Si/SiGe quantum dot devices. Finite-element simulations show that compressively stressed TiN films can generate shear strains exceeding 0.1% at the quantum well, sufficient for deterministic valley splittings of hundreds of $μ\text{eV}$ in strain-assisted Wiggle Wells. We show that this strain can extend across multiple quantum dots and is maintained in realistic gate geometries, providing a fabrication-compatible approach for scaling deterministic valley splitting to quantum dot arrays.

Quantum Physics.title: What Can Actually Be Proved About the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen Paradox? Operational Consistency, Locality, and Quantum Completeness
Quantum Physics.summary: The Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) argument concerns whether accurate quantum predictions imply a complete description of physical reality. We distinguish predictive adequacy, operational no-signalling, EPR elements of reality, and ontological completeness. We formalize the EPR reality criterion using observable-, value-, and context-dependent predicates and prove that its incompleteness implication does not entail a prohibition on objectively stochastic origins of outcomes. A two-observable stochastic-source countermodel establishes this limited logical non-entailment, without addressing randomness generated at measurement or reproducing the full quantum assemblage. We illustrate the latter distinction using an established two-setting qubit steering inequality. For continuous variables, we derive inferred-variance and Gaussian-steering criteria for a stipulated instantaneous elastic-collision map, studying mass ratios, incident wave-packet spreading, covariance inflation, and readout noise. We distinguish losses of fixed-axis Reid violations from losses of optimized Gaussian steering. These results are conditional benchmarks, not predictions for the proposed finite-duration ion-collision apparatus, whose scattering dynamics and preparation and measurement parameters remain unspecified. We also show why uncertainty inequalities and exponential decay memorylessness alone do not establish intrinsic ontological randomness. The analysis delimits the logical and physical assumptions needed for claims about EPR completeness without proposing a new hidden-variable dynamics.
Quantum Physics.comment: 21 pages, 24 references, software code. This article substantially extends and supersedes the initial four-page comment published as arXiv:2604.13135v1 on 14 April 2026

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operator and Separation of Variables for BC-type open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ spin chain
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We construct two-parameter Baxter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators for the transfer matrices of noncompact open $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$ BC-type spin chains with general boundary interactions, treating both one-boundary and two-boundary models. The $\mathbb{Q}$-operators are defined as traces of general monodromy matrices over infinite-dimensional auxiliary spaces carrying principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{C})$.
  At specific values of parameters the two-parameter $\mathbb{Q}$-operators degenerate into simpler one-parameter Baxter operators. We prove that the general transfer matrices factorize into products of these one-parameter $Q$-operators. We provide both an algebraic derivation based on local operator identities and a diagrammatic proof using Feynman diagrammatic techniques.
  Finally, we apply the quantum Separation of Variables (SoV) method to the spectral problem of the one-boundary transfer matrix. We derive the system of separated difference equations for the transfer matrix eigenfunctions and show that, under the assumption of kernel factorization, it reduces to a one-dimensional difference equation coinciding precisely with the Baxter equation for eigenvalues of appropriately normalized one-parameter Baxter $Q$-operator.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Critical behavior of the bosonized Schwinger model with uniform matrix product states
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Quantum electrodynamics in two spacetime dimensions, also known as the Schwinger model, admits a dual formulation in terms of a non-compact boson field. Using a Hamiltonian lattice discretization of the bosonized model, we compute the critical mass of the continuum Schwinger model at $θ=π$. We numerically obtain the ground state on an infinite chain by the variational uniform matrix product state (VUMPS) algorithm, preserving charge conjugation exactly. As a truncated basis for the local Hilbert space, we employ the oscillator basis that diagonalizes the one-site reduced density matrix of the free limit. We constrain the fitting functions for the continuum extrapolation using the Symanzik effective theory for lattice corrections. Our result for the critical mass, $(m/g)_c = 0.333\,555(5)$, agrees with recent staggered-fermion determinations at comparable precision.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holographic Wilsonian RG of Yang-Mills theory in AdS
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this work, we extend the equilibrium-evolution duality between stochastic quantization and Wilsonian renormalization to non-abelian gauge theories in anti-de Sitter space, for which the radial coordinate of AdS plays the role of the stochastic time. We show, to all orders in the fields for bulk theories without explicit radial dependence, that the Langevin distribution at time $t$ is the product of the ultraviolet and infrared radial wavefunctions at the cutoff $ε=t$. We therefore identify this Langevin process as the ground-state (Doob) transform of the radial evolution. By explicit calculation, we also extend the existing dictionary in the stochastic-renormalization duality: the radial component of the bulk field is Zwanziger's stochastic gauge-fixing function; radial gauge is Parisi-Wu quantization; and the bulk gauge $A_z=α^{-1}\partial_iA_i$ is Zwanziger's gauge. We also obtain the expressions for the triple-trace and quadruple-trace couplings of the holographic Wilsonian action at finite cutoff in closed form; in the infrared, they reduce to the known gluon correlators and, at the total-energy pole, to flat-space Yang-Mills amplitudes as expected. Although our explicit results are provided at tree-level and derived in AdS$_4$, we also comment on the de Sitter counterpart of these statements and on the loop corrections.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant. In four spacetime dimensions, the standard AdS-invariant boundary conditions set the rescaled magnetic field to zero for electromagnetism and the rescaled magnetic Weyl tensor to zero for Einstein gravity on the conformal boundary. We generalize these standard boundary conditions by setting arbitrary linear combinations of the electric and magnetic fields, or the corresponding Weyl tensors, to zero, and we conjecture that these exhaust the local, AdS-invariant, conservative boundary conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$. Boundary conditions with non-AdS-invariance and in different spacetime dimensions are also studied. The AdS-invariant conditions in AdS$_{1,3}$ extend to Yang-Mills theory and nonlinear gravity in a general Fefferman-Graham setting. We construct phase spaces for these general boundary conditions. The covariant phase spaces for general conditions are naturally associated with Lagrangians containing Pontryagin terms and, in gravity, a Gauss-Bonnet term. In gravity, except for the standard boundary condition, no nontrivial asymptotic symmetries exist and all conserved charges such as ADM mass vanish identically, as in a closed universe. Spacetimes with Killing fields including AdS then exhibit linearization instability in the sense of Fischer and Marsden and Moncrief. For nonstandard boundary conditions, the modified symplectic structure yields new expressions for the entropy formula of black holes.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 32 pages, no figures; v2: significantly strengthened results on linearization instability of AdS$_{1,3}$, references added; v3: minor revisions

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Higher operator product expansions in twisted non-Lorentzian field theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Twisting theories with super-Poincaré symmetry yields topological-holomorphic field theories, whose operator product expansions of local operators can have as coefficients not only ordinary functions but also `derived' functions with nonzero cohomological degree, described by certain elements of sheaf cohomology. Twisting non-Lorentzian supersymmetric theories yields richer phenomena, where topological and holomorphic spacetime coordinates coexist with ordinary (that is, neither topological nor holomorphic) spacetime coordinates. We propose a sheaf-cohomological description of such OPE coefficients for quantum field theories with arbitrary numbers of topological, holomorphic, and/or ordinary spacetime dimensions, and identify necessary and sufficient conditions for the proposed OPE coefficient space to contain nontrivial `derived' functions; in particular, theories with one topological spacetime dimension and multiple ordinary spacetime dimensions provide a smooth analogue of the (holomorphic) raviolo. We then demonstrate that two-point functions in topological twists of free supersymmetric non-Lorentzian field theories appearing in the literature define nontrivial derived functions consistent with our sheaf-theoretic construction.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 23 pages, 2 figures. Extensive revision with explicit non-Lorentzian examples

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Anti-periodic Gravitino and Dirac Effective Operators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Introducing a preserved $U(1)_R$ symmetry forbids gravitini Majorana masses while allowing a Dirac mass. We investigate how a Dirac mass for gravitini can be described by an effective operator in $N=1$ superspace, in analogy with the well-known Dirac gaugino mass. We find that the corresponding spin-$3/2$ bilinear operator can be expressed in terms of gauge-invariant gravitino curvature superfields coupled through a nonlocal kernel involving an inverse d'Alembertian. We study this construction in minimal five-dimensional supergravity compactified on $S^1/\mathbb Z_2$. The gravitino satisfies anti-periodic boundary conditions induced by a Scherk-Schwarz twist. The physical Kaluza-Klein Dirac masses then appear as poles in the two-point functions of the curvature superfields associated with sources localized at the endpoints. Separation of physical and gauge modes relates these propagators to a quadratic fermionic kernel represented by a $16\times16$ matrix. Its elements match the fermionic components of two invariants written in $N=1$ superspace, including their spinor contractions and normalization. This matching is carried out on a fixed background with a nonzero radion auxiliary field.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Non-Standard Interactions and Light Z' Bosons from CEvNS Data at CONUS+
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We analyze the first Conus+ reactor-antineutrino spectrum to constrain nonstandard neutrino interactions (NSI) with quarks and light vector $Z'$ mediators in $E_6$ and leptophilic $U(1)_{L_a-L_b}$ models. The prediction includes coherent elastic antineutrino--nucleus scattering (CEvNS) and elastic antineutrino--electron scattering (EvES), with Standard Model (SM)--mediator interference in each channel and an analytically profiled normalization uncertainty. We formulate $L_e-L_μ$ and $L_e-L_τ$ in a common charge convention, combining direct electron scattering with the nuclear interaction induced by photon-- $Z'$ mixing. The data remain compatible with the SM. Electronic scattering has little effect on the quark-NSI and fixed-coupling $E_6$ angular regions, but substantially strengthens the low-mass coupling limits of the $E_6$ benchmarks. The leptophilic models share a common low-mass plateau dominated by electronic scattering, while their limits separate at larger mediator masses through their different nuclear loop contributions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. This version corresponds to the accepted manuscript. 23 pages, 6 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Electric birefringence in Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The fermion sector of the pseudo-quantum electrodynamics is integrated functionally to generate a non-linear electrodynamics, that it is called Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics. A non-local Chern-Simons topological term is added to the original lagrangian of the pseudo-quantum electrodynamics in which a most complete electrodynamics gauge invariant in 1+2 dimensions is proposed. As consequence of the fermionic sector, we obtain a non-linear contribution in the electromagnetic fields that breaks the Lorentz symmetry due to Fermi velocity. From the Euler-Heisenberg pseudo-electrodynamics, we study the properties of the plane wave propagating in a planar medium under an uniform and constant electromagnetic background field. The properties of the planar material are discussed through the electric permittivity tensor and magnetic permeability, that are functions of the frequency, wavelength and of the background fields. The dispersion relations and the refractive index are calculated in the presence of a uniform magnetic field, and also in the case only of an electric background field. The birefringence phenomenon emerges only when the electric background field is considered.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 10 pages, no figures. Accepted version in Nuclear Physics, section B

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Silent Heavy Fields: An Exclusion Rule for the Cosmological Collider
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The cosmological collider uses oscillatory signatures in primordial correlators to probe heavy fields during inflation. This probe has blind spots, as heavy fields can keep ticking in time while remaining silent in the correlators. In this letter, we derive an exclusion rule under which cosmological collider signals vanish. The rule covers two classes of diagrams where a de Sitter invariant heavy sector couples covariantly to a single external field at one vertex. We first prove it for exchanges mediated by the two-point function of the heavy sector to all loop orders, using a spectral decomposition followed by a field redefinition. The result then extends to one-loop polygons by matching their oscillatory contributions onto those of the first class. The approximate signals of previously studied processes that fall into these classes must therefore be revisited. As a nonvanishing example, we derive the leading signal of a triangle loop for the first time in a toy model motivated by chemical potentials.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Amplifying the Cosmological Collider with Ghost Spectators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Ghost inflation is a well-known framework in which cosmological fluctuations can generate enhanced primordial non-Gaussianity, typically of the equilateral type. In its original form, however, it is in tension with current observational constraints. Here we instead consider a setup in which a standard inflaton drives the background evolution, while excitations of a ghost condensate act as spectator fields that interact with the inflaton. This proposal fits naturally within the cosmological collider program: the exchanged particle has a modified dispersion relation, $ω\propto k^2$. We show that this ghost-inspired dynamics weakens the usual Boltzmann suppression, similarly to models with a very small effective sound speed, yielding an enhanced bispectrum signal relative to standard cosmological collider scenarios. At the same time, the horizon-crossing scale remains a free parameter of the theory. As a result, the model shares features of both the de Sitter bootstrap and boostless frameworks. Finally, we derive the differential equations governing cosmological correlators in the ghost-collider setup. Their structure reflects the quadratic momentum dependence of the dispersion relation and distinguishes this scenario from conventional relativistic cases.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Self-Force and Bremsstrahlung in Finite Electrodynamics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the self-force and the accompanying Bremsstrahlung for a moving point charge in nonlinear electrodynamics with finite self-field and self-energy. The self-force in the Maxwell theory has been the subject of many studies, often by renowned physicists. After reviewing Coleman's lucid treatise for Maxwell among them, we wish to explore the same question in the Born--Infeld theory, our prototype. We independently compute the local self-force and the global radiative dissipation, and show how the two are mutually consistent. Despite the nonlinearity turning off for the asymptotic radiative field, its residual effect survives via the effective multipole moments of a moving charge, allowing deviation from Maxwell. We close with a detailed discussion about two different manifestations of the self-force in the literature and how these enter our computation. One of the appendices explores Born--Infeld ModMax as a generalization.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Fortuitous ABJM Operators as Black Holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Given a superconformal gauge theory at a fixed loop order, BPS states can be studied in two ways --- by enumerating cohomology classes of a nilpotent supercharge or by diagonalizing the anomalous dimension matrix. The second one allows for a deeper look at how holographic theories distinguish between operators based on whether they are dual to horizonless geometries or black holes. To this end, we carry out the diagonalization in $\mathrm{U}(N)_k \times \mathrm{U}(N)_{-k}$ ABJM theory with $N$ as a formal parameter. This makes it possible to define trajectories of operators and focus on the fortuitous ones which are characterized by being BPS at only finitely many values of $N$. In contrast to $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills, where it has been numerically prohibitive to study more than one of these, ABJM gives us access to 16 such trajectories along with their descendants. We show that they take an especially simple form at large $N$ where they agree with the predictions of integrability. We also show that many of them, as with black holes, can only be dressed by certain types of gravitons and comment on how this exercise in cohomology also has implications for properties of the full operators. Finally, we show that the gap to the first non-BPS state in ABJM theory qualitatively differs from that of $\mathcal{N} = 4$ Super Yang-Mills in the expected way.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 64 pages, 15 figures, v2: Added corrections and a discussion of generalized monotonicity

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Extension of Poincare superalgebra via hidden symmetries
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Isometries of a manifold and special types of spinors called Killing spinors which are related to Killing vector fields constitute a symmetry superalgebra structure corresponding to Poincare superalgebra. The antisymmetric generalization of Killing vector fields to higher degree forms which are called Killing-Yano forms are considered. The odd part of the Poincare superalgebra is extended from the space of Killing vector fields and their rotational representation to the space of special odd Killing-Yano forms and special even closed conformal Killing-Yano forms. The even part is again corresponds to the space of Killing spinors. By defining the relevant brackets, we show that hidden symmetries and Killing spinors together define an extension of the Poincare superalgebra.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Magnetic-slope crossovers in the QCD bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: How a magnetic field alters dissipation in quark--gluon matter is almost unconstrained from first principles, since real-time transport is not directly accessible to lattice simulation. Using a top-down MQGP-inspired M/string-theory construction of a QCD-like thermal plasma, together with a kinetic-theory identity within a specified single-mode quasiparticle truncation and a compatibility construction using available lattice equation-of-state data, we propose a normalization-insensitive sign prediction that the field slope of the longitudinal bulk-to-shear viscosity ratio ζ_\parallel/η_\parallel reverses sign twice with temperature---below and above the deconfinement pseudo-critical temperature T_0, at T_1<T_0<T_2 (the lower reversal T_1 conditional on a stated pion-gas rate inequality). A kinetic-theory identity with phase-appropriate carriers, a quark--gluon plasma above T_0 and a chiral pion gas below, reproduces the same pattern, and lattice speed-of-sound data can be shown to be consistent as well. The bottom-up VQCD in the deconfined phase supports a negative slope for large temperatures; the slope crossover is not resolvable from the available ζ_\parallel/s, η_\parallel/s plots.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 6 pages main + 12 pages supplemental material, 5 figures, LaTeX

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Monopole crystal and effective theory for a monopole-enhanced 3D U(1) gauge theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Recently, a version of U(1) lattice gauge theory on the cubic lattice with a monopole enhancement term was considered in the literature. In this work, we further our understanding of this theory with a mixture of analytical and numerical methods. We show that for sufficiently large monopole enhancement, the monopoles are no longer dilute and they arrange themselves into an antiferromagnetic, Néel-ordered ground state. Nonetheless, a variant of Polyakov's argument for the dilute excitations over the dense ground state leads to an effective sine-Gordon model which is qualitatively similar to that of the standard theory. We also predict analytically the presence of first-order transitions as the monopole chemical potential is varied at fixed gauge coupling, corresponding to a change in the dominant monopole charge. Similarly, we predict a transition in the Ising universality class as the gauge coupling is varied. We then use numerical methods to study the phase diagram of the theory and check some of our predictions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact Infrared Triangle in Gravity with Long-Range Interactions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Einstein gravity coupled to massless matter exhibits universality in the infrared. In the presence of long-range interactions we show that a novel superrotation charge conservation is equivalent to the massless limit of the classical logarithmic soft graviton theorem, and we propose a formula for the corresponding tail to the displacement memory. These results, which extend earlier work on gravity coupled to massive matter in a qualitatively different way, are exact in the gravitational coupling and reveal that long-range gravitational dressings resum. We also compute higher-order corrections to the known superrotation charge which are exact in the gravitational coupling and would correspond to a 1-loop exact correction to the Cachazo-Strominger subleading soft graviton theorem.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of Rényi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 39 pages, 3 figures, v2: rewriting of Sec. 3.1, correction of typos, and improved wording

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: U(1)-Symmetric Spin SYK Models: Ordering, Chaos, and Transport
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model provides an analytically controlled setting for strongly interacting quantum dynamics and holography, but its fermionic formulation leads to nonlocal encoding overheads on qubit-based quantum processors. We study a U(1)-symmetric spin analogue of the complex SYK model, constructed from random charge-conserving $q$-spin interactions that are native to a qubit Hilbert space. In the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, the model reproduces the leading saddle-point structure of complex fermionic SYK under the identification of chemical potential with magnetic field and charge density with magnetization. We investigate the finite-$N$, finite-$q$ regime using exact diagonalization. A U(1)-invariant ordering susceptibility increases with system size for $q = 2, 4$ but decreases for $q = 6$, while bulk-spectrum level statistics are consistent with the Gaussian orthogonal ensemble at half filling and the Gaussian unitary ensemble in the adjacent magnetization sector. We further construct coupled-cluster chains and obtain domain-wall dynamics consistent with diffusive magnetization transport in a small-cluster regime accessible to matrix-product-state simulations. These results establish analytical benchmarks and finite-size signatures of ordering, quantum chaos, and magnetization transport in U(1)-symmetric spin-SYK models, and they motivate quantum simulation of the low-temperature, large-system regime, which remains difficult for classical methods.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Subsystem Flow: Quantum Error Correction, Petz Recovery, and Ergodic Inclusions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In quantum error correction (QEC), the goal is to engineer an encoding that protects logical information against the erasure of a physical subsystem. In local many-body quantum systems, by contrast, nature provides a subsystem inclusion $\mN\subset \mM$ in a fixed reference state $\ketΩ$. Asking whether the inclusion admits a reference-preserving code that protects subsystem $\mN$ against erasure of the complement is equivalent to asking whether $\mN$ is preserved under the modular dynamics of $\mM$ in this state (modular autonomy). We define the subsystem flow, which measures the departure from this error correction regime. Away from autonomy, the infinitesimal flow quantifies relative-entropy loss, while the history algebra and persistent core describe which observables the modular orbit generates and retains. We call an inclusion ergodic when modular orbits generate everything and retain nothing. Analytic continuation of subsystem flow yields Petz recovery maps and a family of positive inclusion parent Hamiltonians. We show that, in general, evolving with these parent Hamiltonians allows $\mN$ to leave $\mM$, and in some cases, it can generate the entire $\mM\vee\mM'$. Inclusions with a common cyclic and separating vector generate everything, and standard inclusions of factors, such as those of nested subregions in QFT, are ergodic. Moreover, the $L^2$-nuclearity property implies that the spectrum of parent Hamiltonians is discrete. We define a dissipative semigroup by repeating the Petz recovery map, whose fixed-point algebra is the modular persistent core and whose spectrum is gapped under the assumption of $L^2$-nuclearity. We conjecture that the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of inclusion parent Hamiltonians can be used to define local spectral measures of quantum chaos.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cubic Curvature Deformations to the Kerr Black Hole Shadow
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the effects of cubic curvature corrections on the shadows of rotating black holes within the effective field theory of gravity. Starting from a perturbatively corrected Kerr metric incorporating two independent cubic curvature couplings, we construct black hole shadows through numerical integration of null geodesics, without assuming separability of the geodesic equations. Using a Hamiltonian ray-tracing approach, we systematically examine the dependence of the shadow geometry on the higher-curvature couplings, black hole spin, and observer inclination. We find that cubic curvature interactions can produce discernible deviations from the Kerr shadow, modifying its apparent size and shape. In particular, the two cubic interactions exhibit distinct effects on the shadow boundary, with the magnitude of the deviations depending sensitively on the coupling strengths and black hole spin. We validate our numerical results through independent convergence tests of the geodesic integration and shadow-boundary determination, and recover the analytical Kerr shadow in the vanishing-coupling limit. Our results provide a complementary probe of higher-curvature gravity in the strong-field regime and illustrate the potential of black hole shadow observations to constrain departures from general relativity.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia: do they bind?
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the existence of molecular two-glueball bound states, so-called glueballonia, in pure Yang-Mills (YM) theory. We mainly concentrate on the scalar and pseudoscalar channels, thus studying scalar-scalar and scalar-pseudoscalar bound states, respectively. Near the onset of binding, when a bound state first appears just below threshold, a nonrelativistic framework is justified. We employ an attractive scalar-exchange Yukawa potential together with a smeared contact term contribution and determine the critical attraction required for binding. For two scalar glueballs, we use the scalar dilaton effective theory to determine the parameters of the non-relativistic potential: the Yukawa interaction is generated by t- and u-channels involving the exchange of one scalar glueball, while the repulsion emerges by the s-channel annihilation and contact interaction. Using lattice-YM input to fix the dilaton parameters, we find that the attraction is strong enough: the scalar glueballonium binds, and the result is quite robust with respect to parameter variations. In a minimal scalar-pseudoscalar extension, the Yukawa attraction is again given by the t-channel scalar glueball, while the crossed u-channel pseudoscalar exchange induces an attractive local contribution, making the pseudoscalar glueballonium also bind in pure gauge. Importantly, both the scalar and pseudoscalar glueballonia are stable in the YM vacuum. Next, we briefly comment on the pseudoscalar-pseudoscalar, scalar-tensor, and tensor-tensor channels: all these channels are attractive too and could form bound states, which, however, would be unstable in pure YM due to decay into two lighter glueballs. Finally, as a cross-check, our formalism confirms that Higgs-Higgs bound state does not form.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cosmological Dressing Rules for Massive Scalars
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation of de Sitter correlation functions comes in different guises including harmonic analysis and dressed flat space correlators. We observe that these are equivalent spectral representations of the same Sturm-Liouville problem. Starting from the latter we derive dressing rules for scalar fields of arbitrary mass with auxiliary propagators in the form of Euler integrals that are accessible to flat space diagrammatic tools.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cosmological correlators and kinematic flow on complex Hartle-Hawking saddles
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Lorentzian gravitational path integral over homogeneous and isotropic metrics in a closed universe with positive cosmological constant is dominated by complex saddle points, such as the Hartle-Hawking saddles. We ask how to compute cosmological correlators on such complex backgrounds, and how they respond to the shifts of the kinematic variables---the kinematic flow---without tracking the bulk time evolution explicitly. We, specifically, study a conformally coupled scalar test field with a cubic interaction around these saddles. We find that the wave function coefficients can be written as discrete spectral sums with the summands containing the corresponding coefficients in the Einstein static universe, which are obtainable in analogy with the polytopes program for flat spacetime. Whereas the wave function coefficients of the flat FLRW case are given by integrals over shifted kinematics, the discrete spectrum on the three-sphere for Hartle-Hawking saddles produces sums. We identify the coefficients, which depend on the final hypersurface through a phase fixed by its size, with Srivastava-Daoust multi-variable hypergeometric functions. They satisfy recursion relations for any number of sites, under which the sums collapse into rational functions. For the one- and two-site Feynman-Witten tree diagrams, we derive difference equations in the kinematic variables which close on a finite set of sums, giving a discrete kinematic flow. The transformation matrices are upper triangular with rational elements, and satisfy a consistency condition which makes the flow path independent. We then obtain the two-, three- and four-point cosmological correlators. At the late-time conformal boundary, we derive an explicit difference equation for the four-point function.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: $α'^2$-corrections to the bosonic string from an action-level double copy map
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The low-energy effective action of the bosonic string contains higher-derivative corrections of the form Riem$^2$ and Riem$^3$ to the Einstein--Hilbert action, together with the associated Kalb--Ramond couplings. We construct an action-level double copy description of these corrections up to cubic order in the fields. Two ingredients are required: a higher-derivative gauge-theory Lagrangian, which up to field redefinitions is controlled by a single $F^3$ coupling, and a deformation of the color-to-kinematics replacement of the structure constants by the corresponding three-momentum tensor. We show that no higher-derivative gauge-theory operator can produce the Riem$^3$ vertex with the standard replacement rule, and that the matching conditions for the gauge-theory coupling and the deformation of the map admit a unique solution, a double root, which renders the cubic action left--right symmetric, of the form $(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)\otimes(\mathrm{YM}+F^3)$. Without further input, the resulting map reproduces the cubic $\mathrm{Riem}\,H^2$ coupling of the bosonic string at order $α'$, the absence of six-derivative cubic Kalb--Ramond couplings at order $α'^2$, and the absence of interactions odd in the Kalb--Ramond field. The comparison is performed in transverse-traceless gauge, up to field redefinitions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: V1: 19 pages. Human verifications done with Cadabra (code available upon request)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Crystalline Equivalence Principle for Anomalies
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a microscopic characterization of crystalline symmetry anomalies in bosonic lattice systems in (1+1) and (2+1) dimensions with a combination of crystalline and finite unitary internal symmetry. We construct anomaly indices of symmetry operators and derive their cocycle conditions and coboundary ambiguities. For generalized crystalline symmetries combining permutations of onsite Hilbert spaces with quantum cellular automata, anomaly indices take values in $H^3(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ and $H^4(B\widetilde Γ,U(1)_r)$ respectively, where $\widetilde Γ$ is the total group of crystalline and internal symmetries, and the coefficient twist $r$ accounts for spatial orientation reversal. When crystalline symmetries act solely by permuting onsite Hilbert spaces, the anomaly classes restrict trivially to the spatial subgroup. These results establish a crystalline equivalence principle for bosonic anomalies at the microscopic level, without assuming a continuum description or emergent Lorentz invariance. We prove that a nontrivial total anomaly index obstructs any symmetric invertible phase. The framework incorporates modulated symmetries where spatial symmetries permute internal symmetries. Our results reproduce LSM and SPT--LSM constraints, with the latter illustrating how spectral-sequence differentials can trivialize candidate LSM anomaly indices.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Swing Surfaces in AdS/CFT
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study holographic entanglement entropy in the flat limit of AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, and clarify the relation between Ryu-Takayanagi surfaces and the swing surfaces proposed for flat-space holography. We show that the ordinary RT formula does not admit a well-defined flat-space limit and connect this to subtleties of the state-operator map in the flat limit. We then construct an AdS$_3$ uplift of the swing prescription and develop its corresponding information-theoretic interpretation through two complementary approaches. First, we show that the swing surface length computes the mutual information between suitably chosen nearly null boundary intervals in a special class of pure CFT states. The gravity interpretation of this result involves scattering processes which take place deep inside of the AdS$_3$ bulk. Second, we reduce the problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation for swing surfaces to the more general problem of finding an information-theoretic interpretation of black hole inner horizons in holography.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Universal Theory of Strange and Bad Metals from Spatially Random Interactions with Underdamped Quantum-Critical Bosons
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: One of the most important challenges in condensed matter physics is understanding the macroscopic properties of strange metals, particularly why their resistivity remains linear in temperature over several decades. We propose that a (2+1)d theory of fermions coupled to underdamped quantum-critical bosons through a spatially disordered interaction provides this long-sought-after theoretical explanation. The key novelty of our work is to establish the appropriate separation of scales so that the bosons are underdamped. Using this framework, we obtain two distinct forms for the fermionic self-energy: a conformal-limit solution, $Σ\sim\sqrtω$, and a marginal Fermi-liquid solution, $Σ\simω\log(1/ω)$, corresponding to regimes above and below the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, respectively. These solutions produce Planckian scattering, exhibit exact $T$-linear resistivity, $ω/T$ scaling in the optical conductivity, as well as $\sim T\log(1/T)$ heat capacity at low temperatures. Moreover, our theory naturally unifies strange- and bad-metal phenomena within a single framework, suggesting that we are now approaching a new epoch in understanding the physics of strongly correlated matter.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Main text: 12 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary Materials: 30 pages, 6 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Isolated Critical Points for Scherk-Schwarz Compactifications of M-theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider Scherk-Schwarz compactifications of M-theory (toroidal compactifications with a non-trivial spin structure) in various dimensions and find isolated critical points of the potential on the moduli space. We demonstrate this by identifying the unbroken duality group and finding isolated points on the moduli spaces which are fixed by elements of the unbroken duality group. We work out concrete examples involving compactifications down to $d=8,6, 5$ and $4$ spacetime dimensions. We also conjecture a duality covariant anomaly cancellation condition for M-theory on $T^n$ orbifolded by discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ symmetries acting as phases on the charge lattice. This anomaly cancellation condition generalizes the level matching requirement for perturbative string orbifolds.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The three-loop QCD helicity amplitudes for $V$+jet production at hadron colliders in full color
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the three-loop Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) corrections to the production of a vector boson $V=Z,W^\pm,γ^*$ and a jet in quark-antiquark annihilation and its kinematic crossings, retaining full dependence on the number of colors. By expressing the infrared-finite remainders in terms of a small set of rational and special functions, we find that the amplitudes live in a strongly restricted function space, compared to the full space of the related Feynman integrals. We provide fast and reliable evaluation in all kinematic regions using numerical transport.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 10 pages, 3 figures. Electronic files with results are available under https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24143650. Numerical evaluation package is available under https://github.com/vjet3loop/Vjet3loop

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Integrable Singularity Black Holes without Inner Horizons in Asymptotically Safe Inspired Gravity and NFW Dark Matter Effects
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate an alternative ultraviolet (UV) structure for Renormalization Group improved (RG) black holes within a phenomenological framework inspired by asymptotically safe gravity. In several regular RG constructions, regularity at the origin is associated with a dS core and an additional inner horizon, raising issues of spacetime predictability and possible mass inflation instabilities. Motivated by this problem, we relate the RG scale to the radially weighted effective quantum gravitational source entering the volume integrand of the quantum corrected Ricci scalar. This prescription yields a Bessel type running Newton coupling with $G_I(r)\sim r$ in the UV, rather than the usual $G(r)\sim r^3$ behavior, and supports an integrable central singularity. The inner branch is matched through the Israel Darmois conditions to an exterior RG solution with $G_{II}\to G_0$ in the infrared, where $G_0$ is the Newton constant. Within the numerical range investigated, the resulting geometry has a single event horizon and no additional inner horizon. We then incorporate an NFW dark matter distribution coupled to the same running coupling. Since $ρ_{\rm NFW}\sim r^{-1}$ while $G_I(r)\sim r$ near the origin, the effective matter contribution entering the field equations remains finite, producing a cored effective behavior without modifying the NFW profile by hand. The gravitational decoupling algorithm keeps the quantum gravitational and dark matter sectors separately conserved within the same geometry. For the configurations considered, the NFW sector shifts the event horizon while preserving the single horizon structure. Thus, the same running coupling governs both the integrable UV black hole geometry and the softening of the central gravitational response of the NFW source.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: How to find regular black-hole islands in the swamp
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: An infinite tower of higher-curvature corrections is expected to lead to regular black-hole solutions. We assume that this regular behavior does not abruptly arise, but gradually builds up with each successive order of the effective field theory of gravity. In addition, we assume that the effective field theory comes with a single scale of singularity-resolving new physics. We translate this assumption into a monotonicity requirement for deviations of the metric functions from a Schwarzschild black hole. Under these assumptions, conditions can be formulated which trace the increase of ``less singular'' black-hole behavior on and outside of the black-hole horizon within the regime of validity of the effective field theory. These conditions constrain the effective field theory coefficients. To exemplify this construction, we motivate five specific conditions and find a corresponding island of black hole regularity conditions at order eight in the effective field theory. We also explore whether string theory as well as asymptotically safe gravity lie on this island.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 29 pages plus appendix and references. 6 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Harmonic superspace and Kaluza-Klein reduction
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We extend the Kaluza-Klein reduction procedure to the framework of harmonic superspace and apply it to the construction of off-shell superfield formulations of supersymmetric gauge multiplets. The reduction is implemented by a deformation of the harmonic derivatives by mass terms, while ensuring that manifest off-shell supersymmetry and Grassmann analyticity are preserved at all stages. As a first application, we reduce the free \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Maxwell theory and obtain an off-shell superfield description of the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive vector supermultiplet. The resulting formulation naturally incorporates an analytic Stückelberg-type gauge symmetry. We then reduce linearized \(5D,\mathcal{N}=1\) Poincaré supergravity and derive the unconstrained harmonic-superspace action for the BPS \(4D,\mathcal{N}=2\) massive supergravity multiplet. The technical simplicity of the procedure stems from the structure of gauge theories in harmonic superspace, where the gauge symmetry is naturally encoded in analytic prepotentials and harmonic derivatives. The approach presented in this paper opens a direct route to gauge-invariant off-shell superfield formulations of massive higher-spin $4D,\mathcal{N}=2$ BPS multiplets. Furthermore, the resulting theories can be reformulated in $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ superspace, opening the way to gauge-invariant off-shell descriptions of $4D,\mathcal{N}=1$ massive higher-spin theories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Radiative stability of species-separated Kaluza--Klein spectra in warped geometry
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Species-dependent fifth-direction lightcones, generated by scalar-gradient operators, can separate gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein (KK) scales in a warped extra dimension, as recently shown by Randall and Riojas. In this work, we study whether this separation survives quantum corrections. Quark loops can only move the gluon speed within the interval spanned by the bare speeds. Gluon exchange pulls the quark speed toward the gluon speed, with a one-loop coefficient strongly enhanced by fifth-component exchange when the gluon is the slow species. We set the size of this effect using the strong-coupling estimates for a light-gluon benchmark, where a $5.5$~TeV gluon sits below quark partners at $10.74$~TeV. Within the effective theory, the Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes then correct the quark speed at order one. That correction is several times larger than the mass ordering can absorb, so the light-gluon ordering has no perturbative protection. The reverse benchmark, with slow quarks and a heavy gluon, keeps its ordering roughly ten times more robust.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum and classical thermal equilibrium for probabilistic classical fields
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The time evolution of the probability distribution for classical fields can be described by the quantum formalism. For free classical fields the free quantum field theory arises as a subsystem. Different probability distributions for classical fields correspond to the classical thermal equilibrium with the Rayleigh-Jeans divergence or the quantum thermal equilibrium with the Planck spectrum. The selection of the Rayleigh-Jeans or Planck spectrum is not a question of fundamental concepts. It becomes an issue of dynamical selection once interactions are present. We compare the momentum dependence of the classical energy and field correlations for the classical and quantum equilibrium. This permits to decide which equilibrium is selected as a result of asymptotic dynamics by numerical simulations of the probabilistic classical fields including interactions. For free probabilistic classical fields we construct a general ``classical-quantum map'' between the classical probability distribution and the density matrix of the quantum field theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Dressed Fock Spaces in Gauge Theory and Gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Four-dimensional gauge and gravitational theories exhibit long-range interactions that require asymptotic particles to be dressed by clouds of soft photons and gravitons. Faddeev-Kulish dressings render scattering amplitudes infrared-finite, but the resulting multi-particle states do not factorise into tensor products of dressed one-particle states. We show that this loss of Fock-space factorisation is not fundamental, but reflects an inappropriate choice of infrared variables. The real soft divergence is reproduced by the Goldstone modes of asymptotic symmetries, while the Coulomb phase is reproduced by new zero modes of the radiative fields that we introduce here. In these variables, infrared-finite dressed multi-particle states admit the usual Fock-space factorisation into single-particle dressed states.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 11 pages, 1 figure; v2: fixed minor typos

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups, given one named hypothesis that is a theorem of that library, so that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.05.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 5 pages. Lean library, book and short version: https://github.com/Fedor-Popov/Lean_VOA (release v1.05)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^μ_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 59 pages, 11 figures, and 5 tables, minor changes

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Vacuum Displacement Principle: Theoretical Framework and Local Phenomenology
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a modified gravitational framework in which the standard Einstein field equations are sourced by a classical matter sector coupled to a Higgs-type scalar field $χ$ modeling a dynamic vacuum substrate. By introducing a phenomenological covariant coupling we implement a physical displacement principle where massive baryonic matter drives the vacuum field away from its vacuum expectation value. We show that this coupling leads to a field-dependent modulation of a particle's inertial rest mass alongside a spatial fifth force, yielding localized violations of the Einstein Equivalence Principle while preserving universal free fall for fundamental point masses. In the weak-field, non-relativistic limit, this interaction manifests as a Yukawa-type correction to the Newtonian potential. We test the viability of this framework against local gravitational constraints, including planetary perihelion precession and Eötvös parameter limits. Finally, we model the steady-state, non-relativistic spherical accretion of dust, demonstrating that the competing effects of vacuum-induced mass modulation and fifth-force acceleration yield distinct density and velocity profiles.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($θ_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($τ_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $γ$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Substantially revised version with updated results, 33 pages, 15 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A Holographic Model for Soft Photons and Gravitons in Four Dimensions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a two-dimensional action on the celestial sphere that describes the infrared sector of Abelian gauge and gravitational theories in four dimensions. In particular, we use the holographic model to reproduce (1) antipodal matching conditions for the superphaserotation and supertranslation Goldstone modes in four dimensions, (2) leading soft photon and graviton theorems, and (3) infrared factorization of amplitudes with generic dressed $in$ and $out$ states. Using (3), we reproduce the infrared divergences that plague the standard undressed amplitudes, and show that amplitudes involving Faddeev-Kulish dressed states are infrared finite. As a corollary, we use our holographic model to construct an infinite class of dressed states that give rise to infrared finite scattering amplitudes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Critical L-values and genus-zero Gromov--Witten invariants
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We establish a period comparison for a two-dimensional rational Hodge summand of type $(3,0)+(0,3)$ in a smooth projective threefold over $\mathbb Q$ with $h^{3,0}=1$. Given an algebraic projector onto the summand and a correspondence whose action on the motive of a rational weight-four newform is nonzero after projection to the summand, restriction to the holomorphic de Rham lines identifies motivic morphisms with maps between these lines. Fixing rational generators of the holomorphic de Rham lines determines a unique isomorphism of homological motives. Its Betti realization then yields an exact relation between geometric periods and two critical modular $L$-values. For the Fermat sextic, we construct the correspondence over $\mathbb Q$ and compute its Betti and de Rham actions, determining the scale from algebraic traces and cup-product pairings. Critical-value evaluations and, under mirror comparison and explicit continuation hypotheses, a continued genus-zero Gromov--Witten partition identity follow as corollaries.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A Toy Model for Topological Entanglement Features in 1+1D Integrable Quantum Field Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper we investigate an entanglement measure, the Rényi entropy, in a 1+1D integrable quantum field theory known as the Federbush model. This is a deformation of the theory of two massive Dirac fermions by means of a bilinear term in the $U(1)$ currents that couples the two fermion species. This deformation gives rise to $S$-matrix elements which are coupling-dependent phases, distinct from -1. These non-trivial phases can be seen as encoding anyon-like statistics. From this viewpoint, the Federbush model is a toy model for topological features of entanglement in one space dimension. In this paper we show that, a standard computation based on form factors of branch point twist fields leads to the conclusion that these topological features play no role when computing most known measures of entanglement at equilibrium in the ground state. This conclusion applies also to the post-quench dynamics at first order in perturbation theory, after a small quench of the topological parameter.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 17 pages. Additional justification for the chosen form factor solutions in v2

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Triple-Massive-Exchange Bispectrum of Quasi-Single-Field Inflation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The triple-exchange bispectrum of the scalar quasi-single-field inflation model has resisted analytic evaluation across its full parameter space since its advent, despite rapid progress in cosmological collider physics. In this Letter, we solve it for general mass and mixing strength as a convergent double series, by applying the Mellin-Barnes representation directly to the mixed propagator between the massless and massive modes. The result is exact, non-perturbative, and physically transparent; the method is broadly applicable.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entropy and charge transport limit Mpemba preparation in holography
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study Mpemba relaxation and its preparation cost in a holographic superconductor with full backreaction. At matched final energy and charge, boundary drives can reverse the ordering of the remaining horizon entropy after source removal. In separate numerical comparisons, some protocols reach a given tolerance earlier even when driving and waiting times are included. To examine the limits of preparation, we consider critical states that already carry a slow scalar field and exterior charge. Along the critical slow branch at fixed energy and charge, horizon displacement cancels the quadratic area response, leaving an entropy reserve of $O(\varepsilon^4)$ for an initial scalar amplitude $\varepsilon$. The same coefficient connects this reserve to the entropy advantage of the nearby superconducting equilibrium and the entropy weight of the slow tail on the normal side. This limited reserve constrains how quickly the existing field can be removed. For releases that suppress the leading horizon field and exterior charge, the preparation time grows at least as $\varepsilon^{-2}$ under horizon regularity and uniform radial control. Charge transport constrains the same covariant scalar flux that produces horizon entropy, raising the minimum flux cost and strengthening the time bound.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Enhanced Early Structure from Axiodilatons & 21cm Observations
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Axiodilatons provide a promising unified model of the Dark Sector whose properties are motivated by the use of accidental approximate symmetries to embed the light fields needed for observations into well-motivated UV physics in a technically natural way. These models turn out to help ameliorate many current puzzles in $Λ$CDM phenomenology (e.g. the Hubble tension and the evidence for evolving Dark Energy) `for free' despite not being designed for that purpose. We here explore in more detail another serendipitous feature of these models: their tendency to enhance early structure formation, in a way that seems suggestive given the accumulating evidence for structure arising earlier than expected in $Λ$CDM. Since early structure growth is the cleanest to study we explore in detail the expected 21cm signal produced by axiodilaton models, using the same parameter choices that improve agreement with observations elsewhere in cosmology. For fixed astrophysics, we forecast that SKA1-Low could distinguish dilaton couplings as small as a few times $10^{-2}$ from $Λ$CDM at $2σ$, mainly because of the earlier formation of structure. We provide complete derivations of the mass dependence of the relevant cosmological observables, including how dilaton-dependent baryon and electron masses affect the hyperfine transition, the Ly$α$ coupling, X-ray heating and ionization during cosmic dawn and the epoch of reionization. We provide details of radiative transfer, atomic physics and the equations governing the thermal and ionization state of the intergalactic medium.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: Conditions for a Local Type IIB D3-D7-D3 Mechanism of Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate the conditions under which a local Type IIB D3$_+$-D7-D3$_-$/E3 configuration can generate perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Assuming the required charged zero-mode spectrum, neutral instanton measure and non-vanishing charged disk amplitudes, we derive an E3-induced chiral mass term with scalar and pseudoscalar components. The latter reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. This yields a conditional matching to the two-sheeted operator within the effective field theory. A separate orbifold example checks the charged zero-mode representations and the compensating instanton charge. Whether all the required instanton ingredients coexist with two independent massive D3-D7 matter sectors at separated endpoints in a single local configuration remains open. We outline a model-building roadmap toward such a configuration and its compact phenomenological embedding. Such an embedding requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 27 pages, 2 figures. Improved title, abstract and conclusion. Manuscript accepted for publication in The European Physical Journal C

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Schwinger-Unruh Interplay and Mode-Resolved Entanglement of Charged Scalar Fields in Rindler Spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study pairwise and cross-horizon correlations of a charged scalar field in Rindler spacetime in the presence of parallel electric and magnetic fields. The transverse magnetic field produces Landau levels, while the longitudinal mode problem follows the charged-scalar Rindler construction with the effective mass $M_n^2=m^2+(2n+1)|qB|$.
