High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The derivative expansion (DE) provides a useful approximation to the Casimir interaction energy between two close surfaces. It has the form of a local functional, obtained from a zero momentum expansion. However, when the system involves a massless field satisfying Neumann conditions, that expansion may develop nonanalytic terms. We present here a study on how this property reflects itself in the need to add to the DE some novel, nonlocal terms. These are, we argue, akin to the ones introduced in effective theories because of the presence of massless particles in loops. We pinpoint the mode responsible for this effect, and construct the effective action due to its fluctuations, showing that it reproduces known nonanalytic contributions, and present the corresponding nonlocal addition to the DE. We also predict a new nonanalyticity: Neumann conditions in $3+1$ dimensions at zero temperature produce a term of order $|{\mathbf k}_\shortparallel |^3$, with a parameter-free coefficient, between the (local) second and fourth orders of the expansion. We show that, for a cylinder in front of a plane, the zero-mode loop adds to the local expansion a term of relative order $(L/R)^{3/2}$, with a coefficient that we compute explicitly, showing that it accounts for the behaviour of the existing numerical fits for that geometry.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Towards a foundation model for Type IIB flux vacua
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Progress in characterising the Type IIB flux landscape requires scalable methods for constructing flux vacua. In this work, we investigate generative models as a framework for sampling vacua across multiple Calabi-Yau geometries and for directing searches towards specified physical properties. We compare transformers and diffusion models trained to generate quantised fluxes together with approximate values of the complex structure moduli and axio-dilaton. We exploit a staged training procedure comprising pre-training, and post-training via reinforcement learning, and assess how each stage improves the generated distributions and enables targeted sampling. We further examine whether structures learned from geometries with smaller $h^{1,2}$ can be transferred to geometries with larger $h^{1,2}$ through fine-tuning on specialised datasets. Our results provide evidence that generative models can learn distributions of flux vacua across distinct compactifications, improve searches for vacua with selected properties and transfer information between geometries. This establishes a concrete basis for developing a foundation model of the Type IIB flux landscape.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quasinormal Modes and Environmental Trapping around Charged Letelier Black Holes with Perfect-Fluid Dark Matter and Quintessence
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the massless scalar quasinormal spectra of charged Letelier black holes surrounded by logarithmic perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and quintessence, for $Λ=0$ and for asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, together with the test Maxwell spectra for $Λ=0$. For $Λ=0$, sixth order WKB values with Padé resummation agree with independent time domain evolutions to within $0.06\%$ for the fundamental modes. Stronger string cloud and quintessence lower both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates, while a larger charge or a larger positive PFDM parameter $β$ raises both. In our convention $β>0$ means negative PFDM energy density; negative $β$ gives a positive density and reverses the shift. The angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit reproduce the eikonal trends and approximate the $\ell=2$ WKB frequencies at the percent level. For $Λ<0$ the scalar potential diverges at the AdS boundary and the single barrier WKB formula does not apply. We therefore solve the eigenvalue problem with a Chebyshev pseudospectral method in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with regularity at the horizon and a Dirichlet condition at the boundary, and check the modes against time domain evolutions and Schwarzschild-AdS benchmarks. The AdS spectrum contains long-lived modes trapped between the photon sphere barrier and the reflecting boundary, with damping rates spanning about five orders of magnitude. The damping correlates with the ratio of the oscillation frequency to the barrier top frequency, consistent with leakage through the barrier. No growing modes are found in the test field sectors and parameter ranges studied, which does not establish the stability of the fully coupled system.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A geometrical invitation to BMS group theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In these lecture notes, a group-theoretical introduction to BMS symmetries is provided in a self-contained manner. More precisely, all definitions and structures are purely based on geometrical and group-theoretical notions defined at null infinity and valid in any dimension (four or higher), in a way that circumvents its traditional bulk realisation as asymptotic symmetries. The topics which are reviewed are: the definition of BMS transformations as conformal Carrollian isometries of null infinity, the semidirect structure of the BMS group, the holographic reconstruction of Minkowski spacetime in terms of good cuts, the one-to-one correspondence between good cut subspaces and Poincaré subgroups (aka vacua), as well as a basic introduction to the unitary representations of the BMS group.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v1: 40 pages; v2: 50 pages, typos fixed, Figure 3, Section 6, and Appendix A.6 added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: On $ι$Quiver (BPS) Algebras and (Strict) Partitions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider the $ι$quiver algebras of split type associated with the quiver BPS algebras of affine type A. They are supposed to give twisted affine Yangians and (elliptic) $ι$quantum toroidal algebras that could possibly arise from D-branes on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_n$ with orientifolds. We mention some properties of these algebras, such as the minimalistic presentations in the rational cases and the coideal structures. We also investigate how one might identify these algebras from the quiver theories with orientifold actions. Moreover, we discuss some representations with combinatorial bases of these algebras. In particular, the algebras with $n=1,2$ in certain limits of the parameters have representations labelled by (coloured) strict/symmetric partitions, which in the case of $n=1$ recovers the known BPS counting of certain theories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The non-asymptotic flatness of the charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics as well as the quantum statistical relation automatically satisfied, but also both the Christodoulou-Ruffini relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: typos corrected, references added, presentation refined

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Wilsonian renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $κ_τ\Barψσ_{μν}F_{μν}ψ$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields a nontrivial fixed point with~$e_*=0$, $κ_*\neq0$, and~$γ_A=-1$. This fixed point has three relevant directions, as does one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line, in particular the additive mass renormalization proportional to~$κ^2$, eliminate this fixed point unless $N_f$ is at least several tens; for~$N_f=1$ there is no fixed point at weak Pauli coupling. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$, $κ_τ$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value~$κ_{\text{ind}}(e_τ)$, which is proportional to~$e_τ^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_τ^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Algebraic instantons and non-Gaussian vacuum in quantum mechanics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The standard instanton calculus in quantum mechanics is based on harmonic minima in the potential. When the perturbative vacuum is anharmonic, $V\simeqλx^{2n}$ with $n\ge2$, the standard construction fails. We study this problem for a particle on a circle and subject to a potential $V(x)=16λ\sin^4(x/2)$. The instanton and its fluctuation operator are known in closed form, but they differ qualitatively from the familiar ones. Because $V''=0$ at the minimum, the classical vacuum is gapless, the instanton decays algebraically (an algebraic instanton), the zero mode is located at the threshold of a continuous spectrum, and the one-loop determinant is infrared divergent. Quantum mechanics generates a non-perturbative gap $E_q\propto\hbar^{4/3}λ^{1/3}$, and the instanton is embedded in a vacuum that is dynamically gapped, similar to what happens in Yang--Mills theory. We show that the one-instanton amplitude can be computed by matching the instanton trajectory to the exact vacuum part of the path integral. The resulting prefactor scales as $\hbar^{4/3}$, and this expression agrees with the numerical spectrum to a very high accuracy. The classical interaction between instantons decays as $T^{-3}$, whereas the correct result is an exponential decay controlled by the dynamically generated gap, beyond the quantum time scale. We provide an alternative derivation of this result based on a sum over intermediate states.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $χ_{π^0}-χ_σ$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $χ_{π^0}-χ_{δ^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_π\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Diagonally gauged anomaly-free 6D supergravities and their vacua
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study anomaly-free six-dimensional $N=(1,0)$ supergravities with $n_T=1$ and diagonal $U(1)_{R+}$ or $Sp(1)_{R+}$ gauging. The diagonal group combines R-symmetry with a commuting action on hypermultiplets. We perform bounded searches for anomaly-free models with one or two additional simple gauge group factors of rank at most 30, impose string-charge lattice and positive kinetic term conditions, and tabulate the resulting spectra. The main scans cover $q_{\max}\leq2$ and $d_{\max}\leq3$, where $q_{\max}$ is the largest absolute hyperino charge and $d_{\max}$ the largest diagonal $Sp(1)$ representation dimension, with supplementary searches at larger values. Every hypermultiplet block is required to be nontrivial under at least one additional simple gauge factor. The search has led to a large number of models. Here we give the details of 93 models with $G_+= U(1)_{R+}$ and $q_{\rm max}\le 2$, and 26 models with $G_+=Sp(1)_{R+}$ and $d_{\rm max}\le 3$, and one or two simple group factors. Additional 1341 and 494 models with $G_+=U(1)_{R+}$ with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $Sp(1)_{R+}$ with $d_{\rm max}=3$, respectively, are posted to the GitHub repository. We establish the existence of supersymmetric Minkowski vacua for all the anomaly free models we have found with $q_{\rm max}=2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$. We find that such vacua require $q_{\max}>1$ for $U(1)_{R+}$, and $d_{\max}>2$ for $Sp(1)_{R+}$. We also show that every Minkowski vacuum breaks R-symmetry, with the connected unbroken gauge group contained in the additional gauge factors. At two-derivative order, while our anomaly free models do not admit AdS$_6$ solutions, all those with $q_{\rm max} = 2$ and $d_{\rm max}=3$ have non-supersymmetric and unstable dS$_6$ vacua as well.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 55 pages, major revision, errors corrected, model scan substantially extended

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact SU(2) Yang-Mills Waves from a Simple Ansatz
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We use an ansatz based on rotations of the Pauli basis to construct exact propagating solutions of the sourceless SU(2) Yang--Mills equations in $(3+1)$ dimensions. By examining and extending this ansatz, we obtain two wave families with nontrivial transverse structures and a family of finite-amplitude waves on a self-similar non-Abelian background. These solutions can retain a genuinely non-Abelian structure while admitting arbitrary wave profiles propagating at the speed of light and carrying the corresponding longitudinal electric or magnetic fields. We also investigate the parameter conditions for their non-Abelian character and their energy transport. For the self-similar family, we study the structure of its singular plane and construct suitable sources to replace the singular region while preserving wave propagation in the remaining regions. This offers a possible interpretation of these solutions as propagating fields outside sources.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entanglement and Charge Transfer
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the entropic order parameter introduced in (1905.10487) using the replica trick for two disjoint intervals. For a global symmetry, this quantity measures the mutual information carried by charge-anticharge intertwiners. We formulate the problem in terms of averages over twisted partition functions on replica Riemann surfaces, and obtain exact solutions for free fermions and compact bosons, for $U(1)$ symmetry and its discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroups. We show that further averaging over both families of non-contractible cycles gives access to an additional quantity, which is the loss of Holevo information associated with complementary-charge measurements that occurs upon removing the intertwiners. For the boson, this quantity vanishes, whereas for Dirac fermions it equals the difference between the mutual information of the fermion-parity-gauged and ungauged theories, independently of the choice of even $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroup. Finally, we extend the analysis to non-Abelian symmetries using saddle expansions, deriving universal behavior in the nearly touching intervals limit and for a large number of fermions $N_F\gg1$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Phase Structure and Thermodynamic Geometry of STU Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the thermodynamics of four-dimensional STU black holes, a family of charged solutions of gauged N = 8, SO(8) supergravity, from the perspective of geometric thermodynamics. We focus on non-rotating solutions carrying pairwise-equal charges, obtaining closed-form expressions for the thermodynamic quantities directly in terms of the physical charges, and use them to determine the equation of state and associated phase structure. We also construct the Ruppeiner geometry for the STU black hole, taking the temperature and thermodynamic volume as fluctuation variables, and study its renormalized curvature as a probe of the black hole microstructure. We find a rich phase structure with two critical points present whenever the charge ratio is sufficiently large, and identify regions in parameter space associated with attractive and repulsive microscopic interactions.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Off-shell one-loop counterterms of Palatini gravity with an independent background connection
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We compute the one-loop divergences of pure gravity in the first-order (Palatini) formulation, using the background field method in Goldberg variables, with a background connection independent of the background metric. Background Ward-Takahashi identities are verified at one loop. The divergences of the two-point functions, obtained in arbitrary dimension and gauge, require, besides the curvature-squared terms, invariants built from the nonmetricity of the background connection; in particular, the Gauss-Bonnet combination, which is not topological for a nonmetric connection, does not suffice. Three- and four-point functions in the Feynman-de Donder gauge complete the counterterm Lagrangian up to fourth order in the nonmetricity and provide parameter-free tests of it. All the counterterms vanish on shell, as in the metric formulation, and off shell they can be removed by field redefinitions.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $η\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $η$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $η=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$. For nested families of clusters, this degeneracy structure naturally organizes into a space of rooted trees. Subtracting the divergence gives a renormalized mass matrix which extends smoothly to every stratum of the Axelrod--Singer compactified moduli space $\overline{M}{}^{\,\mathrm{AS}}_\ell= \overline C_{\ell-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)/\mathrm O(n)$ and splits naturally into one mass matrix per vertex of the bubble tree.
  Geometrically, at each vertex carrying punctures the suitably rescaled metrics converge to a complete scalar-flat metric with the nodes filled in, adjacent such pieces being joined by Schwarzschild necks, and the renormalized matrix acting as its mass data. For $n=3$, the necks contain minimal spheres, which are common apparent horizons of the merging holes. At vertices bearing two holes, we determine on which side of the limiting horizon each node lies, and we formulate as a conjecture the resulting criterion for a neck to be a component of the outermost horizon. We also compare the mass lower bound of Part~I with the Riemannian Penrose inequality. Because the mass matrix is invariant under rotations of the bubbles, it lives on a Deligne--Mumford-type quotient of the compactification.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear and quadratic gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity and general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory, the dimension, and the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile, or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$ dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We compare the two considered theories and study relations between their solution sets. We further examine conformal relations, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and so is the Weyl squared action (that reduces to Weyl conformal gravity in $n=4$), as a particular example of quadratic gravity couplings. Explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Another Look at the Weak-Field Limit of Generalized Hybrid Metric-Palatini Gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the weak-field regime of generalized hybrid metric-Palatini theories, described by a generic function \(f(R,\mathcal{R})\), where \(R\) is the metric Ricci scalar and \(\mathcal{R}\) is constructed from an independent torsionless connection. Linearizing the field equations about Minkowski spacetime, we show, without using the scalar-tensor representation, that the theory propagates the usual massless spin-2 mode and two massive scalar modes, with an effective gravitational coupling. The absence of tachyonic and ghostlike instabilities at the linearized level, together with the nondegeneracy of the scalar sector, is shown to impose algebraic restrictions on the derivatives of \(f(R,\mathcal R)\) evaluated on the Minkowski background, which generalize previously obtained conditions. The Newtonian limit for an extended static source is derived, yielding a gravitational potential with two Yukawa corrections whose amplitudes are fixed by the scalar residues, while finite-size effects are encoded in source-dependent form factors. We determine the conditions under which the usual Newtonian limit is recovered and derive the effective post-Newtonian parameter \(γ_Σ\) governing light propagation. Finally, we compute the radial epicyclic frequency and the corresponding anomalous periapsis advance, and compare it with planetary precession data to constrain the parameters of a viable hierarchical scalar-mass regime.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Revised version accepted for publication in the European Physical Journal C

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Gravitomagnetic Bootstrap: from Newtonian gravity to general relativity via localizing rotational and conformal symmetries
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Newtonian gravity, in the light of the Equivalence Principle, is best understood as a localization of Galilean inertial structure --- or at least, of the part of Galilean inertial structure that defines rectilinear acceleration. I consider what kind of theory can be constructed if we also localize rotational inertia and spatial and temporal scales. The resultant theory, given weak assumptions, is unique up to a constant with the dimensions of velocity and an overall sign. For an appropriate choice of these, it coincides with the first post-Newtonian approximation to general relativity, so that this construction gives a method to bootstrap from Newtonian gravity to general relativity without explicitly presupposing special relativity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Energy-flow bubbles at the Schwarzschild horizon and their Regge-pole clock
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: For a circularly polarized plane wave scattered by a Schwarzschild black hole, the time-averaged energy flow on the side of the horizon facing the wave contains small, sealed recirculation cells. In the main family, pairs of zero circles are born on the axis and slide into the horizon in periodic frequency windows; at higher frequencies further cells appear off the axis. We map the cells for $κ=ωr_s/c\le10$ and show that each is the interference of a background integral with the leading photon-sphere Regge surface wave. A cell can die only at a zero of the circularly polarized field on the horizon, and all sixteen measured deaths are such zeros. A parabolic-cylinder analysis at the top of the potential barrier reduces this to a phase condition with a constant $π/4$ and no fitted parameter; recorded before the measurement, it predicted eight deaths in $6\leκ\le10$ to within 0.012 in $κ$. Electromagnetic duality makes the core of each main-family cell a circle of linear polarization; inside such a cell, flow lines lie on nested tori and close into torus knots of one chirality.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 22 pages, 5 figures, 16 tables; the Letter is followed by the Supplemental Material in the same file

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact transformation-optics representation of the Ellis wormhole and limits of finite-device scattering emulation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We derive a global isotropic representation of the ultrastatic Ellis wormhole and establish which features of its electromagnetic response can, and cannot, be reproduced by a finite device. An orientation-preserving coordinate map sends the signed proper-radial line to a punctured Euclidean chart with refractive index $n(ρ)=1+a^2/(4ρ^2)$. Through the Plebański correspondence, this gives the exact impedance-matched continuum medium $\varepsilon_r=μ_r=n(ρ)\mathbf{I}$ and its full vector-Maxwell operator. For the ideal two-ended geometry, we derive the electromagnetic radial operator, establish its spectral properties, and express its scattering amplitudes through Jost solutions and Wronskians. Nonzero transmission into the second asymptotic end implies $|R_{\rm id}|<1$ at every real frequency, whereas a regular, lossless finite one-port has unit-modulus reflection. The reverse triangle inequality therefore yields a strictly positive lower bound on the complex reflection-amplitude mismatch. This theorem applies to the stated lossless single-port class and is not extended to lossy or multiport realizations. We compute converged multipole scattering data and establish the low-frequency threshold scaling $|T_L|^2\propto(ωa/c)^{4L+2}$, with coefficients independently validated for $L=1,2,3,4$. The transmission cross section tends to $πa^2$, while the ideal profile's total scattering cross section has a logarithmic forward divergence. We also construct a smooth finite-shell target and derive an exact finite-band constitutive-error formula for a calibrated passive Lorentz model. The constitutive benchmark is kept distinct from scattering equivalence throughout.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. v2: references to earlier work on wave scattering, grey-body factors and observational tests of wormholes added. Ancillary files contain the Python and MATLAB codes and the data needed to reproduce all figures and tables

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Casimir-like wormholes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate spherically symmetric spacetimes sourced by matter with energy density $ρ\propto 1/r^{4}$ and equation of state $p_r = ωρ$. We derive the most general solution of Einstein's equations for this class of sources, obtaining black holes, naked singularities and traversable wormholes, parametrized by the integration constants and $ω$. We show that only two classes of matter can support traversable wormholes: Casimir-type matter with $ω> 0$ and phantom matter with $ω< -1$, while quintessence and conventional dark energy are excluded by the flare-out condition. For the Casimir value $ω= 3$, the transverse pressure approaches $p_t \to -ρ$ near the central singularity, so the full algebraic structure of the Casimir stress-energy tensor, $ρ\propto -1/r^{4}$, $p_r = 3ρ$, $p_t = -ρ$, is not imposed but emerges from Einstein's equations. Treating the amplitude of the energy density as a free classical parameter, we obtain wormholes with throat radii from microscopic to astrophysical scales. These Casimir-like configurations share the functional form of the Casimir tensor but are not generated by the physical Casimir effect; Garattini's Planck-scale Casimir wormhole is recovered when the quantum Casimir energy scale is imposed. The total amount of exotic matter is finite for arbitrary $ω$ and scales linearly with the throat radius. Analyzing the traveler's acceleration, tidal forces and transit times, we show that radial free fall satisfies all human traversability conditions for $r_0 \gtrsim 10^{8}$ m. Finally, embedding diagrams illustrate three geometric regimes depending on $ω$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: SPH methods in the modelling of compact objects
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We review the current status of compact object simulations that are based on the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) method. The first section of this review is dedicated to SPH as a numerical method for Newtonian, ideal gas dynamics and it should be fairly self-contained. It begins with the basics of the method, but also describes recent advances including various meshless derivatives or methods for treating shocks. A separate chapter summarizes general relativistic SPH, including its special relativistic limit, and it explains in some detail the recent development of full numerical relativity in SPH where matter is evolved together with a dynamical spacetime. The remainder of the review has an astrophysical focus, here we discuss the status of the simulations of white dwarf--white dwarf, neutron star--neutron star and neutron star--black hole systems. For each type of system the emphasis is on gravitational-wave-driven mergers, but we also briefly summarize dynamical collisions that can occur in locations with large stellar densities.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Living Reviews of Computational Astrophysics; accepted, completely revised version; 186 pages; first three chapters are a self-contained review of SPH

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gas-induced gravitational-wave dephasing and accretion periodicities of live post-Newtonian massive black hole binaries: warm disk
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We perform 3D hydrodynamical simulations of an equal-mass quasi-circular live $10^6 {\rm M}_\odot$ massive black hole binary (MBHB) embedded in a prograde, locally isothermal circumbinary disk (CBD) with 0.1 aspect ratio. The binary evolves under the effect of gaseous torques and 2.5 post-Newtonian dynamics. We follow the gravitational-wave (GW) driven inspiral from 53 Schwarzschild radii ($r_s$) down to merger, over 1.5 years. Comparing the GW inspiral rate with the viscous inflow, we find the binary to decouple from the CBD just $\approx 2$ days before merger. We measure gas torques (gravitational and accretion) with and without concurrent GW emission, finding that their sums agree to within $\lesssim 5\%$ down to $25 r_s$. We then measure a gas-induced GW phase shift that peaks at $\approx 5\times10^{-4}$ rad near $45 r_s$, as the gas torque slows the inspiral, and then changes sign as the accreted mass accelerates it. It is LISA-detectable only at $z\lesssim 0.1$. We further characterize the mass accretion rate modulations. All three fundamental periodicities, associated with the "lump" at the inner cavity edge, the binary orbital period, and half of it, are shifted to lower frequencies by precession. We measure the shift at the orbital period, due to relativistic apsidal precession, in an inspiraling binary for the first time, and newly identify the other two as due to the precession of the eccentric cavity. Our results have implications for multi-messenger astronomy, since observation of accretion rate modulation by LSST/Roman surveys and phase-shift by LISA will provide crucial information on the complex environment surrounding MBHBs.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Under review at ApJ. Phase shift corrected for accreted mass (sign change during inspiral)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Cosmological implications of $f(T,B)$ gravity: Constraints from recent observations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work, we examine the theoretical framework of modified teleparallel gravity including the boundary term in the action and investigate its cosmological implications for the power-law model $f(T,B)=-T+α(-B)^β$, aiming to address late-time accelerated expansion and dark energy. Here $T$ denotes the torsion scalar and $B$ represents the boundary term, whose presence allows departures from standard teleparallel dynamics and provides a unified description connecting torsion- and curvature-based formulations, reproducing $f(T)$ and $f(R)$ gravity in appropriate limits. The viability of the model is assessed by confronting its predictions with data and constraining the cosmological and model parameters via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) using cosmic chronometers (CC), the Pantheon plus sample (PPS), and DESI baryon acoustic oscillation Data Release 2 (BAO DR2) datasets, and by comparing its performance with the standard $Λ$CDM model. Our results, for the obtained constraints on $β$, strongly indicate that, within the adopted parameterization and prior ranges, the data favor a non-zero correction to the boundary term. The AIC shows that the combined CC+PPS dataset mildly favors the $f(T,B)$ model, suggesting an improved fit to late-time observations over $Λ$CDM, whereas BIC favors $Λ$CDM, since the $f(T,B)$ model is penalized by an extra free parameter from the initial conditions needed to solve the cosmological equations. The model predicts a Hubble constant between the Planck and SH0ES determinations, again consistent with current late-time observations. Background cosmological quantities indicate a dynamical phantom-divide crossing while remaining compatible with observations, yielding a viable expansion history and characteristic dark-energy evolution.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Probing superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational wave observations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate superradiant cloud level transitions in stellar-mass black hole binaries with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations. Under the adopted cloud formation and survival conditions, the $\lvert322\rangle\rightarrow\lvert31-1\rangle$ fine transition can imprint phase corrections in the LISA band, while Bohr transitions occurring after the milli-Hertz band observation can be probed through shifts in the merger time. Modeling the coupled cloud-orbit evolution, we find that cloud depletion can begin before resonance and that ionization can advance rather than delay coalescence. For a representative nearby binary, a vacuum injection-recovery analysis yields a cloud-mass-fraction posterior concentrated at $M_c^i/M\lesssim10^{-6}$. Comparing the LISA-predicted coalescence time with a subsequent ground-based measurement provides a complementary test of later cloud evolution. These results motivate complementary searches for ultralight bosons with milli-Hertz and multiband gravitational-wave observations.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. We then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. We further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in Kerr. Interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. More broadly, our work illustrates how WKB methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 20 pages + appendices, 9 figures, 2 ancillary data files. v2: improved numerical checks for Kerr

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black hole thermodynamics from Iyer-Wald formalism with variable Newton's constant
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Recent advances in black hole thermodynamics have intensified efforts to investigate its thermodynamic framework and analogues to that of classical thermal systems. Departing from the extended phase space approach, which involves a variable cosmological constant, the restricted phase space formalism focusing on the variations of Newton's gravitational constant in black hole thermodynamics is proposed. This approach enables the construction of a self-consistent thermodynamic structure that features both the first law and the Euler relation. In this paper, we demonstrate that for any diffeomorphism-invariant gravitational theory, the Iyer-Wald formalism is applicable to restricted phase space thermodynamics and construct a self-consistent extensive black hole thermodynamic system. Our work thereby establishes the Iyer-Wald approach as the geometric foundation for black hole thermodynamics with variable Newton's constant.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 12 pages; V2:Discussions added,version accepted for publication in EPJC

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quasinormal Modes and Environmental Trapping around Charged Letelier Black Holes with Perfect-Fluid Dark Matter and Quintessence
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We compute the massless scalar quasinormal spectra of charged Letelier black holes surrounded by logarithmic perfect fluid dark matter (PFDM) and quintessence, for $Λ=0$ and for asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes, together with the test Maxwell spectra for $Λ=0$. For $Λ=0$, sixth order WKB values with Padé resummation agree with independent time domain evolutions to within $0.06\%$ for the fundamental modes. Stronger string cloud and quintessence lower both the oscillation frequencies and the damping rates, while a larger charge or a larger positive PFDM parameter $β$ raises both. In our convention $β>0$ means negative PFDM energy density; negative $β$ gives a positive density and reverses the shift. The angular frequency and Lyapunov exponent of the unstable circular null orbit reproduce the eikonal trends and approximate the $\ell=2$ WKB frequencies at the percent level. For $Λ<0$ the scalar potential diverges at the AdS boundary and the single barrier WKB formula does not apply. We therefore solve the eigenvalue problem with a Chebyshev pseudospectral method in ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, with regularity at the horizon and a Dirichlet condition at the boundary, and check the modes against time domain evolutions and Schwarzschild-AdS benchmarks. The AdS spectrum contains long-lived modes trapped between the photon sphere barrier and the reflecting boundary, with damping rates spanning about five orders of magnitude. The damping correlates with the ratio of the oscillation frequency to the barrier top frequency, consistent with leakage through the barrier. No growing modes are found in the test field sectors and parameter ranges studied, which does not establish the stability of the fully coupled system.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A hybrid log-likelihood-ratio statistic for single-detector SPIIR gravitational-wave searches
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Periods with only one detector operating accounted for 13.3 percent of the third LIGO-Virgo observing run (O3) and 29.7 percent of the first part of the fourth observing run (O4a). We present the first dedicated single-detector implementation of the Summed Parallel Infinite Impulse Response (SPIIR) pipeline for binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) merger searches. Our hybrid log-likelihood ratio combines signal-consistency models for non-Gaussian glitches with a profile likelihood ratio for the signal-to-noise ratio under a Gaussian-noise model. We calibrate the glitch model by source category and trigger-rate class. We assign false alarm rates (FARs) using the measured background from the same detector and analysis chunk, extrapolating its high-ranking tail. We check the FAR assignments by comparing observed and expected cumulative background counts for BNS in O3a and NSBH in O3b at LIGO Hanford (H1) and LIGO Livingston (L1). Using O3 data and the GWTC-3 injection set, we find that, at a threshold of one false alarm per two months, the BNS sensitive distances are $136.5^{+2.9}_{-3.0}$ Mpc in L1 and $120.2^{+3.1}_{-3.3}$ Mpc in H1. These central estimates are approximately 24 and 38 percent higher, respectively, than the GWTC-3 GstLAL values of $110.5^{+3.2}_{-3.4}$ Mpc and $87.2^{+3.6}_{-3.9}$ Mpc over the same data and injection parameter ranges. GstLAL provides the only published single-detector results in GWTC-3. For NSBH, SPIIR reaches $164.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc in L1 and $134.9^{+6.3}_{-7.0}$ Mpc in H1, compared with $165.1^{+6.7}_{-7.3}$ Mpc and $156.0^{+5.9}_{-6.4}$ Mpc for GWTC-3 GstLAL, respectively. Targeted searches recover triggers associated with GW190425, GW200105_162426, and GW230529_181500 with assigned FARs below the same threshold.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A geometrical invitation to BMS group theory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In these lecture notes, a group-theoretical introduction to BMS symmetries is provided in a self-contained manner. More precisely, all definitions and structures are purely based on geometrical and group-theoretical notions defined at null infinity and valid in any dimension (four or higher), in a way that circumvents its traditional bulk realisation as asymptotic symmetries. The topics which are reviewed are: the definition of BMS transformations as conformal Carrollian isometries of null infinity, the semidirect structure of the BMS group, the holographic reconstruction of Minkowski spacetime in terms of good cuts, the one-to-one correspondence between good cut subspaces and Poincaré subgroups (aka vacua), as well as a basic introduction to the unitary representations of the BMS group.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: v1: 40 pages; v2: 50 pages, typos fixed, Figure 3, Section 6, and Appendix A.6 added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Multi-throat generalized Ellis--Bronnikov wormholes with asymptotic string-cloud behavior
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study an ultrastatic, spherically symmetric family of traversable wormholes obtained by locally deforming a generalized Ellis--Bronnikov areal-radius profile in a spacetime with an asymptotic angular deficit. Depending on the deformation parameters, the same analytic family contains one, two, three, or four throats. The corresponding bifurcation curves are obtained in dimensionless form, and the resulting geometries are regular and asymptotically conical. We also reconstruct a source in General Relativity using a canonical scalar, a shift-symmetric phantom scalar, and a magnetic nonlinear electromagnetic field coupled to the canonical scalar. In the reference multi-throat geometry, the coupling removes a branch obstruction of an uncoupled single-valued nonlinear electrodynamics (NED); the same obstruction occurs whenever equal values of the magnetic invariant require different values of $\mathcal G_F$. For $\mathcal G(F)=F+λ\sqrt F$, the NED sector carries the leading asymptotic stress, which scales as $r^{-2}$ and approaches the string-cloud equation of state. The total stress tensor satisfies pointwise energy conditions in finite belly-centered regions of representative two- and four-throat solutions, while the throats violate the radial null energy condition (NEC) and the violation extends into integrable asymptotic tails. The Nandi--Zhang--Kumar covariant volume integral of $ρ+p_r$ is quadratic in the deformation amplitude; its zero is distinct from the bifurcation curves. Away from saddle-node boundaries, each throat supports a radially unstable background-metric light ring, and each intermediate belly supports a radially stable one, with an internally trapped null family in the double-throat case. These results place the topology, source reconstruction, integrated NEC content, and background-metric circular-orbit structure in a common parameter-space description.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The non-asymptotic flatness of the charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics as well as the quantum statistical relation automatically satisfied, but also both the Christodoulou-Ruffini relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: typos corrected, references added, presentation refined

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A dual-moment phenomenological framework for gravitational,electromagnetic and strong interactions
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The unification of fundamental interactions remains an outstanding open problem in fundamental physics. Most existing unification schemes rely on extra dimensions, exotic symmetries, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. Here we construct a minimal classical phenomenological framework built on primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic dual moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently formulated within a unified inverse-square-law structure. We postulate a universal coupling relation connecting source-charge couplings and moment-mediated couplings across these interaction sectors. Although weak-charge degrees of freedom can be formally accommodated within the formalism, full quantitative treatment of weak-interaction dynamics is left for future work. The model recovers well-established low-energy limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons. Importantly, it yields distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects, and three independent experimental schemes are proposed to test these predictions.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, Revised title and introduction for clarity. The numerical parameters for the flow experiment are updated to physically realizable values. The core theoretical framework remains unchanged

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Adiabatic particle production in a time-dependent accelerated frame
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. The Klein-Gordon equation separates into a modified Mathieu equation in time and a confining Schrödinger problem in space with a discrete spectrum. We impose an adiabatic vacuum at the instant of maximal acceleration and compute the particle number in the inertial future. For the zeroth-order adiabatic state it falls as the inverse eighth power of the initial mode frequency, and raising the adiabatic order cancels successive terms of the endpoint expansion, in analogy with the switching transients of finite-time detectors. Analytic continuation of the spatial eigenfunctions gives the out modes in closed form and an exact expression for the particle number, which is entirely the mismatch at $t=0$ between the initial state and the out vacuum. The spectrum is algebraic rather than Planckian.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dymnikova black string
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We obtain a new static black string solution of Einstein's equations with a negative cosmological constant sourced by a Dymnikova-type anisotropic matter distribution. At large radial distances, the geometry approaches the Lemos black string, while the behavior near the central region is characterized by an effective curvature parameter. We examine the weak and strong energy conditions, the horizon structure, and the curvature invariants. The Ricci and Kretschmann scalars remain finite at the origin. We also investigate the Hawking temperature and heat capacity, with particular attention to the dependence of the thermodynamic behavior on the Dymnikova scale.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Canonical partition function and equation of state in the heavy quark region of finite-density lattice gauge theory
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We investigate the phase structure and equations of state in lattice gauge theory at finite temperature and finite density, focusing on the canonical partition function obtained by decomposing the grand partition function with respect to particle number. We demonstrate that when quark masses are heavy, the complex phase of the quark determinant, which causes the sign problem, can be controlled by decomposing the grand partition function according to particle number. In this study, we propose an algorithm to calculate the canonical partition function for heavy-quark, high-density effective theory and test it for the first time using one-flavor $SU(2)$ gauge theory, a case where the sign problem arises. When the grand partition function of $SU(2)$ is decomposed into canonical partition functions, the sign problem is serious in odd-particle sectors, while it is mild in even-particle sectors. The odd-particle sectors also expose a fundamental issue: center symmetry makes the canonical partition function of $SU(N_c)$ vanish unless the particle number is an integer multiple of $N_c$. Although appropriate in the confinement phase, this restriction must be treated carefully in the deconfinement phase. We resolve the issue by introducing an infinitesimal external field, calculate the canonical partition functions by Monte Carlo simulation, reconstruct the grand partition function, and determine thermodynamic observables over a wide range of temperature and density. Furthermore, we find that the chemical-potential dependence of the equation of state at low temperatures exhibits behavior characteristic of the hadron resonance gas model, and that no softening of the QCD matter occurs at finite density.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 9 pages,11 figures, Contribution to the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026)

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: HVP contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in spacelike and timelike domains
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: The hadronic vacuum polarization contributions to the muon anomalous magnetic moment $a^{\text{HVP}}_μ$ in spacelike and timelike domains are recapped. The values of $a^{\text{HVP}}_μ$ assessed within dispersively-improved perturbation theory are reported. The obtained results can be employed in the evaluations of $a^{\text{HVP}}_μ$ in the framework of such methods as lattice studies, MUonE project, and others.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Axial-Vector Lattice Benchmarks Reveal a Common Medium Response of Meson Screening in Hot QCD
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Meson screening masses trace the evolution of hadronic correlations toward quasi-free quark--antiquark screening in hot QCD. Combining lattice QCD (LQCD) benchmarks with a symmetry-preserving Dyson--Schwinger baseline, we identify a flavor-dependent axial-vector quasi-free onset, $x^\ast_{fg}=T^\ast_{fg}/T_c$: an operational matching scale based on the proximity of the axial-vector screening mass to its free-field reference, where $T_c$ is the pseudocritical temperature. On the finite interval $1\le T/T_c\lesssim x^\ast_{fg}$, independent light/strange and charm-containing lattice benchmarks are organized by a common medium-response function with one flavor-sector parameter. One axial-vector point fixes this parameter; the remaining axial-vector data test the temperature dependence of the response, and vector screening masses validate it without vector input. A reduced-mass interpolation then yields lattice-testable predictions for quasi-free onset scales and vector and axial-vector screening spectra in light--charm and open-bottom sectors.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Hamiltonian Truncation Framework for Gauge Theories on the Interval
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: In this work, we investigate gauge theories in two dimensions nonperturbatively using the Hamiltonian truncation approach. Working on a spatial interval and adopting the axial gauge, we remove all gauge field degrees of freedom and express the interacting Hamiltonian in the eigenbasis of the free Dirac theory, truncated at a finite energy. As a benchmark we analyse the Schwinger model, where our numerical spectra agree closely with the exact results from bosonization across a wide range of couplings, validating the construction of the Hamiltonian. We then generalize the formulation to nonabelian gauge groups and apply it to SU(3) gauge theory with a single massless Dirac fermion. These results demonstrate that gauge theories can be explored nonperturbatively using a truncated Hamiltonian that generates evolutions in ordinary time, offering a complementary alternative to lattice field theory.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 27 pages, 8 figures. To match published version

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: On reflection positivity of lattice chiral fermions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We point out that the overlap Weyl fermion, the spacetime lattice realization of a Weyl fermion underlying Lüscher's construction of lattice chiral gauge theories, is not reflection positive in two and four dimensions at finite lattice spacing. Consequently, the standard Osterwalder--Schrader reconstruction does not yield a Hilbert space with a self-adjoint Hamiltonian. In two dimensions, we further show that the overlap Weyl fermion cannot be cut open: the lattice action becomes nonlocal in the presence of a boundary, as expected from the gravitational anomaly of the continuum field theory. By contrast, the overlap Dirac fermion is known to be reflection positive. However, its compact axial symmetry is not invariant under the reflection, whereas a reflection-invariant axial symmetry is noncompact, and both are part of an Onsager algebra.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Wilsonian renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $κ_τ\Barψσ_{μν}F_{μν}ψ$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields a nontrivial fixed point with~$e_*=0$, $κ_*\neq0$, and~$γ_A=-1$. This fixed point has three relevant directions, as does one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line, in particular the additive mass renormalization proportional to~$κ^2$, eliminate this fixed point unless $N_f$ is at least several tens; for~$N_f=1$ there is no fixed point at weak Pauli coupling. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$, $κ_τ$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value~$κ_{\text{ind}}(e_τ)$, which is proportional to~$e_τ^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_τ^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Fate of chiral and $U(1)_A$ symmetries in hot QCD matter under background magnetic fields
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We summarize our recent lattice QCD study of chiral and singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking in background magnetic fields. The magnetic field explicitly reduces the non-singlet flavor symmetry through the unequal light-quark electric charges. We therefore study two neutral-channel susceptibility differences: $χ_{π^0}-χ_σ$ for chiral symmetry breaking and $χ_{π^0}-χ_{δ^0}$ for singlet $U(1)_A$ symmetry breaking. The calculation uses fixed-scale $(2+1)$-flavor HISQ ensembles with $m_l=m_s^{\mathrm{phys}}/10$, corresponding to a zero-field pion mass of $M_π\simeq220\,\mathrm{MeV}$. Magnetic fields enhance both susceptibility differences at low temperatures. Near the crossover, sufficiently strong fields instead suppress both differences. The suppression sets in at larger magnetic fields and is milder for the singlet-axial susceptibility difference than for the neutral chiral susceptibility difference.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures; Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: First Lattice Calculation of Structure-Dependent Radiative Corrections to Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Leptonic Decays
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: The ratio of electronic to muonic leptonic decay widths, $R_{e/μ}$, for the light mesons $π$ and $K$, provides a clean test of lepton flavor universality (LFU) and a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. Its Standard-Model prediction is exceptionally precise, with the leading uncertainty associated with the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction of $O(0.1\%)$. As experiments such as PIONEER and NA62 aim for unprecedented precision, this SD correction has become an essential ingredient in precision experiment--theory comparisons. We present the first lattice QCD$+$QED calculation of this SD correction at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. We employ the infinite-volume reconstruction (IVR) method with Coulomb-gauge photons, significantly reducing both statistical errors and finite-volume effects. We obtain the Standard-Model predictions, $R_{e/μ}=1.23516(10)\times10^{-4}$ for $π$ and $R_{e/μ}=2.47661(31)\times10^{-5}$ for $K$. Our results reduce the hadronic uncertainty in $R_{e/μ}$, provide the most precise Standard-Model predictions to date, and establish first-principles benchmarks for future high-precision tests of LFU.

Atomic Physics.title: Hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet $2^{3}S(L = 0)-$state in the two-muonic helium ${}^{3}$He $μ_{2}$ atom
Atomic Physics.summary: The hyperfine structure splitting for the triplet $2^{3}S(L = 0)-$state in the two-muonic helium ${}^{3}$He $μ_{2}$ atom is determined to high accuracy. Such a structure arises as a result of hyperfine (or spin-spin) interaction between the triplet two-muonic shell and non-zero spin of the central helicon nucleus. Our result for the hyperfine structure splitting is $Δ\approx 2.5811701551505 \cdot 10^{7}$ MHz, where the standard uncertainty has been evaluated as $\pm 10$ Hz.

Atomic Physics.title: Parity nonconservation in hyperfine transitions of hydrogen-like muonic atoms
Atomic Physics.summary: We investigate parity nonconservation (PNC) in the $2s_{1/2}(F=0)\leftrightarrow 2s_{1/2}(F=1)$ hyperfine transition of hydrogenlike muonic $^{13}\mathrm{C}^{5+}$ and $^{15}\mathrm{N}^{6+}$. Finite-nuclear-size effects and the Uehling potential are incorporated directly into the Dirac equation, whereas the leading kinematic-recoil and Fermi--Breit hyperfine corrections to the energy levels are treated to first order in perturbation theory. The spin-independent PNC amplitude is evaluated using hyperfine-resolved energy denominators and is proportional to the weak charge $Q_W$. The spin-dependent amplitude is proportional to $κ=κ_a+κ_Z$, where $κ_a$ and $κ_Z$ denote the nuclear-anapole and direct neutral-current couplings, respectively. For absorption we obtain the PNC degree $\mathcal P_{\rm abs}(^{13}\mathrm{C})=-5.9\times10^{-8}Q_W +1.3\times10^{-5}κ$ and $\mathcal P_{\rm abs}(^{15}\mathrm{N})=-8.8\times10^{-9}Q_W -8.1\times10^{-6}κ$. Nuclear-structure calculations indicate that $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ has enhanced relative sensitivity to direct $Z^0$-boson exchange, whereas the spin-dependent interaction in $^{15}\mathrm{N}$ is expected to be dominated by the nuclear-anapole contribution. In an idealized cavity-polarimetry model, a column density of order $10^{15}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}}$ is required; however, the production of metastable hydrogenlike muonic ions remains the principal experimental challenge.

Atomic Physics.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
Atomic Physics.summary: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

Atomic Physics.title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.08E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
Atomic Physics.summary: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18. To our knowledge, this is the first intercity long distance frequency-ratio measurement, whose total uncertainty reaches the level required by the redefinition roadmap. The measured ratio exhibits a significant correlation with Earth tides and its response agree with the model within the statistical uncertainty. At intercity scale, this comparison demonstrates the capability of an optical-clock network for frequency comparison and Earths gravitational-potential sensing, a key step toward a wide-area optical-clock network.

Atomic Physics.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
Atomic Physics.summary: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon.

Quantum Physics.title: Shallow Clifford circuits on square lattices
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the depth of CZ circuits, Clifford state preparation, and Clifford unitary synthesis over the two-dimensional square lattice. A programmable circuit on a $2{\times}k$ ladder ($n{=}2k$) implements an arbitrary CZ computation in depth at most $\frac{3n}{2}{+}3$ up to reversal of both rails. This improves the best-known LNN (Linear Nearest-Neighbor)-compliant depth-$(2n{+}2)$ construction by about 25\%. For state preparation, we consider a Phase gate programmable -H-{CNOT+P}-LC- circuit and derive matching obstructions to attaining the CZ-span counting lower bound of $2\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil{-}1$ for depth by the entangling gates. For cycle connectivity $C_n$, we prove that the minimum depth is exactly $2\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil{-}1$ when $n$ is not a multiple of four and $2\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$ when $n\,{=}\,4k$. We construct a hole-free minimum-perimeter square-lattice patch with a Hamiltonian cycle for every even size, giving optimal-depth programmable circuits to implement Clifford states for all $n\,{=}\,4k{+}2$. Exhaustive and heuristic searches address the remaining cases for $n$ up to 256, and selected values up to 1,024 qubits. The improvement against comparable state-of-the-art, an LNN-compliant depth-$(2n{+}2)$ solution, is about 50\%. Finally, combining state synthesis circuits developed in this work with a known four-diagonal-stage decomposition gives rise to a depth $4n{-}4$ for $n\,{=}\,4k{+}2$ and depth $4n$ for $n\,{=}\,4k$ implementation of arbitrary Clifford unitaries. This improves the most relevant state-of-the-art, an LNN-compliant depth $7n{-}4$ construction, by about 43\%.

Quantum Physics.title: A Numerical Approach to Quantization
Quantum Physics.summary: We introduce a numerical approach that simultaneously searches for matrix quantizations and compatible Poisson structures on classical geometric surfaces. Our method identifies irreducible Hermitian matrix representations and a trainable Poisson multiplier by minimizing a loss function that penalizes violations of the Casimir and commutation constraints. Through numerical investigations and subsequent theoretical analysis, we establish a no-go theorem showing that, for Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres with nondegenerate axial spectrum, the matrix dimension cannot exceed the degree of the nonconstant polynomial axial Poisson multiplier. We further extend our approach to nonpolynomial Poisson multipliers, demonstrating its versatility and potential to drive novel discoveries. Although here we focus on Weyl quantized fuzzy spheres, the framework is extensible to general geometric manifolds and quantization schemes. Our approach also provides a practical starting point for investigating Schild string theory and the quantization of spacetime histories.

Quantum Physics.title: Inverse-Designed Nanobeam Cavities for High-Cooperativity Spin-Photon Interfaces in Silicon
Quantum Physics.summary: Telecom-band spin defects in silicon offer a compelling platform for integrated quantum networks by combining scalable silicon photonics with spin-based quantum memories and multiqubit registers. The T center and recently demonstrated Al1 center are particularly promising, but their limited coherent zero-phonon emission requires strong cavity enhancement for efficient spin-photon interfaces. Here, we inverse-design silicon nanobeam cavities for both centers using a unified adjoint-optimization framework targeting Purcell enhancement, resonance alignment, and photon extraction. For each emitter, symmetric cavities maximize Purcell enhancement, while asymmetric cavities provide directional coupling to an integrated waveguide. Three-dimensional finite-difference time-domain simulations yield loaded quality factors up to 3.25 x 10^6, Purcell factors up to 7.49 x 10^5, and cooperativities of approximately 1.4 x 10^3 to 2.6 x 10^4, corresponding to cavity-coupled emission fractions exceeding 99.9%. The asymmetric cavities direct approximately 90% of emitted power into a single on-chip waveguide while maintaining cooperativity above 1.4 x 10^3. Under nanometer-scale fabrication perturbations, all four designs remain within the high-cooperativity regime, and high cooperativity persists when the cavity quality factor is constrained to a realistic absorption-limited value of 10^5. This unified, fabrication-compatible framework establishes a scalable cavity-design route for silicon telecom spin-photon interfaces and, to our knowledge, the first cavity designs for the Al1 center.

Quantum Physics.title: Latency-Preserving Rewrites and Translation Validation for Dynamic Quantum Circuits
Quantum Physics.summary: A dynamic quantum circuit measures qubits during a run and chooses later operations from the outcomes. These branches make the qubits wait: the outcome must reach the classical controller, and the controller must decide. We present qlin, a compiler that reduces this waiting time. qlin moves operations out of branches without delaying the program, a property proved in Lean 4. For error-correction decoders, which branch on syndromes that are almost always zero, qlin compiles the likely syndromes into one multiway branch and keeps the original program for the rest. A cost model decides when a classically controlled gate should become a quantum-controlled gate instead. On all benchmarks, qlin checks that the compiled program computes what its source computes, and the checker is proved sound in Lean 4. At the published per-decision cost of the QICK controller (42 ns), 10 of 65 programs run at least 10% faster than the best baseline in our cost model, up to 91.2%, mostly because one multiway branch replaces a long chain of if statements. On the register-transfer logic of the QubiC controller, a compiled distance-5 repetition decoder selects its correction in 21.3 instead of 151.1 expected cycles. Timing runs on an IBM device were too noisy to confirm or reject the model's ranking.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose quantum sine imaginary-time evolution (QSITE), a quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of a Hamiltonian. QSITE approximates imaginary-time evolution through an exact sine filter. We give two circuit implementations of this operator: a sequential one that applies it as a concatenation of linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), reusing two ancilla qubits across steps via mid-circuit measurement, and a coherent one based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). A telescoping identity shows the two prepare the same state and succeed with identical probability, differing only in how that probability can be boosted. QSITE belongs to the family of ancilla-based probabilistic imaginary-time filters and we state rigorous convergence guarantees: we prove that the QSITE operator converges uniformly to the exact ITE operator, that the prepared state converges to the ideal ITE state, and that the filter probability increases monotonically with each concatenation step. Although the construction applies to an arbitrary Hamiltonian, we specialize it to optimization Hamiltonians, and this specialization is what exposes its structure more easily. Since MaxCut eigenvalues are integers, the probability of failure is periodic in the evolution time, yielding safe zones, the first located analytically and the second numerically. For MaxCut we further show that, when the tolerated energy error is a fixed fraction of the ground-state energy, the probability of failure can be bounded below 1/2 with concatenation steps growing linearly with the number of qubits in the first safe zone. We present numerical results for random Erdös-Rényi instances with up to 24 qubits and benchmark QSITE against QAOA.

Quantum Physics.title: Chiral Majorana Charge Kondo Criticality
Quantum Physics.summary: Unambiguous identification of chiral Majorana edge modes remains challenging because the transport signatures proposed for them can also arise from conventional mechanisms. Here we identify the chiral Majorana charge Kondo (CMCK) critical point as a more discriminating many-body route to detect chiral Majorana edge modes. This criticality arises in a charged island hosting a single chiral Majorana edge mode, where Majorana self-conjugacy locks normal and anomalous tunneling amplitudes, so that each physical lead provides two Kondo screening channels without fine tuning. Ordinary subgap states generically break this locking and drive the system toward conventional charge Kondo (CK) behavior. In the simplest two-terminal geometry, CMCK and conventional CK share the critical conductance $G^*=e^2/2h$, but their leading conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/3}$ and $T$, respectively. Their residual entropies also differ, as do the crossover exponents under gate detuning and contact asymmetry. For $N$ leads, CMCK conductance corrections scale as $T^{1/(N+1)}$, and for $N\geq3$ even the critical conductance differs from that of conventional CK with the same number of leads. These universal signatures are testable using established charge-Kondo measurement techniques.

Quantum Physics.title: Linear-optical nonlocality without postselection
Quantum Physics.summary: Linear optics is one of the major platforms for quantum information processing and experimental tests of quantum foundations. This motivates a thorough exploration of its capabilities and limitations. In this paper we investigate the extent to which passive linear optics, when fed with single-photon Fock states and followed by postselection-free number-resolving measurements, can demonstrate nonlocality. These resources define BosonSampling, a computational model believed to have intermediate computational power, being neither classically simulable nor quantum universal. We prove that, when restricted to only two input photons, this system also has intermediate nonlocality capabilities, achieving a violation of the CHSH inequality no higher than $1+\sqrt{2}$. Although this value has appeared frequently in the literature as achievable, to our knowledge this is the first proof that it is maximal. We show that, as we increase the number of available photons, linear optics can produce violations arbitrarily close to Tsirelson's bound of $2\sqrt{2}$. Finally, we extend the analysis to tripartite nonlocality, leveraging well-known interferometric suppression laws to show how several tripartite inequalities can be violated in this setup beyond their bipartite bounds.

Quantum Physics.title: Coherent manifolds and quantization
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the differential geometry of coherent manifolds modelled on convenient vector spaces and apply it to coherent quantization. A smooth coherent product determines geometric structures on the label manifold. We construct a common invariant domain for the quantizations of coherent vector fields and of coherent diffeomorphisms with smooth diffeomorphic adjoints. These quantizations are distinguished operators on the associated quantum space and satisfy commutator, covariance, and formal adjoint relations. Their coherent matrix elements can be calculated by differentiation and substitution in the coherent product. Extending the operators to the common invariant domain leaves their Hilbert space closures unchanged. Motions in subgroups of diffeomorphisms give rise to Lie algebras of generators without requiring a Lie group structure on the subgroup. Suitable coherent motions recover the infinitesimal quantization by differentiation. We express quantum dynamics through coherent matrix elements and obtain a coherent action principle by restricting the quantum action to coherent states. For Klauder spaces, the construction gives creation and annihilation operators, the canonical commutation relations, Segal fields, Weyl operators, and normal ordering on the common invariant domain.
Quantum Physics.comment: 52 pages. Substantial revision of "Coherent manifolds". We construct a common invariant domain for finite and infinitesimal quantization by adjoining iterated derivatives of coherent states. We extend the theory of motions to subgroups of diffeomorphisms without assuming a Lie group structure and revise the applications to variational principles and bosonic quantization on Klauder spaces

Quantum Physics.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
